items.title: EFCC arraigns Lagos socialite Tejuosho for alleged N603.4m job scam
items.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Wednesday arraigned a socialite, Halimat Adenike Tejuosho, before the Federal Capital Territory High Court, Gwagwalada Division, for an alleged N603,400,000.00 job scam. She was arraigned before Justice A. S. Adepoju on a five-count charge bordering on advance fee fraud, obtaining by false pretence and criminal conduct, according to a statement posted on EFCC’s X page. Count one reads: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho and Gidado Ibrahim between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court obtained the sum of N603,400,000.00 (Six hundred and three million four hundred thousand naira) from Oluseye Yomi-Sholoye under the false pretence that you will facilitate her appointment as the Group Managing Director, GMD of Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), which pretence you knew to be false and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 1(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006 and punishable under Section 1(3) of the same Act. Count two reads: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did corruptly receive a total of N259,900,000 (Two Hundred and Fifty-Nine Million, Nine Hundred Thousand Naira) proceeds of crime into your Access Bank account with number 0021083069, which sum you knew to be derived from criminal conduct and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 17(a) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004 and punishable under Section 17(b) of the same Act. Count four states: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho on 30th September 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did corruptly receive a total of N50,000,000 (Fifty Million Naira) proceeds of crime into your Access Bank account with number 0021083069 and name HALEEMS INTEGRATED SERVICES LIMITED, which sum you knew to be derived from criminal conduct and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 17(a) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004 and punishable under Section 17(b) of the same Act.” Tejuosho pleaded not guilty to all the charges. Following the plea, defence counsel, Chuks Ugwuru, urged the court to grant the defendant bail on liberal terms, noting that all five counts are bailable offences. He said the application was anchored mainly on her ill health, citing a medical report which, he argued, showed that she was critically ill. “The ill health of an accused person is a consideration worthy enough to be reckoned as a ground of special circumstances,” he said, urging Justice Adepoju to exercise his discretion in the defendant’s favour. Responding, lead prosecution counsel, Yahaya Tarfa, said the EFCC opposed the application and had filed a 12-paragraph counter-affidavit with one exhibit, along with a written address. Tarfa acknowledged that bail is at the court’s discretion but urged that any terms imposed should ensure the defendant is available to face trial. He then submitted the matter to the court’s discretion. Delivering ruling on the application, Justice Adepoju held that the offences are bailable. Relying on the medical reports before the court, the judge admitted Tejuosho to bail in the sum of N100 million, with one reasonable surety in like sum. The court ordered that the surety must reside within the court’s jurisdiction and own land or property in the Federal Capital Territory. The title documents are to be verified at the FCT Land Registry, with a copy deposited with the Registrar of the court. Tejuosho is also to deposit her international passport with the registrar pending the hearing and determination of the charge. The judge ordered that Tejuosho be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre until she meets the bail conditions. The matter was adjourned to February 1, 2027 for trial. In April 2026, the EFCC declared Tejuosho wanted over an alleged case of obtaining money by false pretence. The post EFCC arraigns Lagos socialite Tejuosho for alleged N603.4m job scam appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: HIDAH Foundation provides free healthcare to children and residents in Dodowa
items.description: The HIDAH Humanitarian Foundation has organised a free healthcare outreach at the Home of Taqwa Orphanage in Dodowa, providing medical services to children at the facility and residents of the surrounding community. The exercise was aimed at improving access to basic healthcare, promoting early detection of health conditions and encouraging regular medical check-ups among vulnerable groups. Services provided included general medical consultations, ear, nose and throat (ENT) screening, laboratory investigations, vital signs assessment and general health checks, alongside medical advice. Speaking at the event, the Founder of HIDAH Humanitarian Foundation, Mujahida Ibrahim Prah, said the initiative was intended to bring essential healthcare closer to people who face difficulties accessing medical services. “The goal of this outreach is to bring healthcare closer to people who need it most. We want to ensure that vulnerable individuals and underserved communities have access to essential healthcare services,” she said. Mrs Prah said the Foundation was also seeking to encourage early detection, noting that some people delayed seeking medical attention until their conditions became serious. “We are focused on promoting early detection of health conditions and creating awareness about the importance of regular medical check-ups. Many people wait until their condition becomes serious before seeking help, and we want to change that,” she added. She reaffirmed the Foundation’s commitment to supporting vulnerable people, saying healthcare should be accessible to everyone. “At HIDAH Humanitarian Foundation, we believe that healthcare is a right, not a privilege, and that every individual deserves an opportunity to live a healthy and dignified life,” she stated. Orphanage and residents welcome intervention Caretaker of the Home of Taqwa Orphanage, Waris Alhassan, who spoke on behalf of the children, thanked the Foundation and its partners for extending the outreach to the facility. “We are very grateful to HIDAH Foundation and all the partners for coming to our aid. The children have been checked, and some have received treatment and advice. This means a lot to us,” he said. A resident of the community, Alima Mohammed, said financial constraints had prevented her from visiting a hospital for several months. “I have not been able to go to the hospital for a long time because of money. Today, I was able to see a doctor, do a laboratory test, and get advice, all for free. I am so happy and I thank the organizers from the bottom of my heart,” she said. Schools, health facilities support outreach The outreach was sponsored by Majd International School, with Vaal Real Estate, Delta Diagnostic Centre and Ogbojo Polyclinic serving as partners. Mrs Prah expressed appreciation to the sponsor, partner organisations, healthcare professionals and volunteers for contributing their time, resources and expertise to the exercise. “They gave their time, resources, and expertise, and we are truly grateful. Without them, this would not have been possible,” she said. The HIDAH Humanitarian Foundation has pledged to continue its community health outreach programmes to extend basic healthcare services to more underserved communities.

items.title: Un producteur algérien retire un film sur la Palestine du festival de Marrakech
items.description: La société de production algérienne Issad Film Productions ne souhaite pas qu'un film sur la Palestine, dont elle détient les droits, soit inclus dans la compétition officielle d’un festival cinématographique au Maroc, un pays qui s’enfonce dans sa compromission avec Israël alors que le calvaire des Palestiniens à Gaza et en Cisjordanie se poursuit. Issad Film Productions retire « Chroniques des années de siège » du festival de Marrakech « Chroniques des années de siège », du réalisateur palestino-syrien Abdallah Al-Khatib, a été retiré de la compétition officielle de la 23ᵉ édition du Festival international du film de Marrakech (FIFM). Ce retrait survient à la demande de la société de production algérienne, détentrice des droits de l’œuvre, a indiqué la direction du festival dans un communiqué repris par la presse marocaine, dont le site Yabiladi. La direction du festival de Marrakech a expliqué qu'elle est tenue de respecter la volonté de la société détentrice des droits, d'où sa décision de ne pas maintenir le film dans sa programmation. « Chroniques des années de siège » décrit le calvaire des Palestiniens sous l’occupation israélienne « Chroniques des années de siège », dont le titre est calqué sur le film algérien primé à Cannes en 1975, « Chronique des années de braise » de Mohamed Lakhdar Hamina, évoque le calvaire que vit la population civile palestinienne sous l’occupation israélienne. Le scénario retrace le quotidien de civils palestiniens piégés dans une ville assiégée par l’armée israélienne, et qui doivent faire face aux pénuries et à la peur. « Chroniques des années de siège » a été présenté en février dernier à la Berlinale 2026 et a remporté le prix du meilleur premier long métrage. Il a été aussi programmé dans plusieurs grandes manifestations, dont le festival du film de Londres (BFI), l'AFI FEST de Hollywood et la Mostra de São Paulo (Brésil). La société algérienne Issad Films Productions ne s’est pas exprimée sur sa décision de retirer le film du festival marocain. Il n’est pas exclu toutefois que la décision soit liée aux positions pro-israéliennes des autorités marocaines. L’article Un producteur algérien retire un film sur la Palestine du festival de Marrakech est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: US sanctions Hezbollah-linked charity in push against Iran's proxies, Treasury says
items.description: By Andrea Shalal Nov 18 (Reuters) - The United States on Wednesday issued new Hezbollah-related sanctions targeting three people based in Lebanon, and three entities as part of a broader effort to shut down Iran's proxy networks, the Treasury Department said. Treasury said its Office of Foreign Assets Control designated the Hezbollah-affiliated charity Ta’awanu Association and its founder, along with two Lebanese brothers who the US said have aided the Islamic militant group with a gold- and cash-smuggling network.

items.title: GRIDCo pushes to complete 161kV Kumasi–Anwomaso project to improve power reliability
items.description: The Chief Executive of the Ghana Grid Company (GRIDCo), Ing. Frank Otchere, has inspected ongoing works on the 161kV Kumasi–Anwomaso (K1K2) transmission line, urging the technical team to maintain progress and complete the project on schedule. The inspection took place at the Anwomaso project site as part of his regular oversight of the upgrade, which is expected to strengthen electricity transmission and improve power supply reliability in the Ashanti Region. During the visit, Ing. Otchere engaged the technical team on progress and the execution of the ongoing stringing works. He said the project was important not only for the transmission network but also for households and businesses that depend on a reliable electricity supply. “The K1K2 project is not just about infrastructure; it is about the quality of life for the people of Ashanti Region. I am impressed with the progress so far, but we must not relent. We must deliver this project on schedule and to the highest standard,” he stated. The K1K2 upgrade forms part of GRIDCo’s broader programme to reinforce the electricity transmission network and respond to growing power demand in the Ashanti Region. According to GRIDCo, completing the transmission line works, alongside the installation of transformers, is expected to improve power delivery and reduce supply interruptions associated with the ongoing construction. The latest inspection follows an earlier joint visit by Ing. Otchere and Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr Frank Amoakohene, to key electricity infrastructure project sites, including K1K2. During that visit, the Minister was briefed on ongoing upgrades intended to strengthen electricity infrastructure in the region. Ing. Otchere was accompanied by senior management staff, including the Deputy Chief Executive for Engineering and Operations, Ing. Samed Ibrahim, who also expressed confidence in the project team.

items.title: Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts
items.description: By Chioma Obinna Health experts on Wednesday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular medical checks. The experts, who spoke at the Annual General Meeting/Scientific Conference of the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Ebute-Metta, Lagos, tagged: “ Your Body, Your Responsibility: A Personal Guide to Cancer Risk Reduction for Physicians, lamented that physicians, despite their knowledge of healthy living, often neglect their own health while attending to patients. They called for a deliberate shift towards preventive healthcare among doctors, warning that professional dedication should not come at the expense of their lives. Speaking at the conference, Chief Consultant Cardiologist at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, Dr Folashade Daniel, said doctors must consciously balance their professional responsibilities with adequate rest, exercise, healthy eating and routine medical examinations. Daniel, who spoke on protecting the hearts of physicians, said: “I don’t think physicians can balance their work, healthy living, and their mobility. It has to be intentional.” She noted that doctors sometimes work for extended hours, leaving little time for personal health, but stressed that they must make deliberate efforts to recover and maintain healthy lifestyles. “First of all, know that your life is not just, your life doesn’t just entail your job. You are a person, you have a family, and you have responsibilities. Yes, to your patients, but also to your family, to yourself,” she said. According to her, doctors should make adequate rest, relaxation, healthy eating and physical activity essential parts of their routines, rather than treating them as optional activities. She advised physicians with a family history of cardiovascular disease to exercise extra caution and make annual health checks a priority. “Take your birthday, for example, your one anniversary, to do a check-up. And then look up all the results with a colleague. Don’t just be your own doctors. Let somebody look at what you have, the results you have done, and give you advice as need arises,” Daniel said. The cardiologist also urged government to strengthen policies that promote healthier food choices and safer working environments. She identified excessive salt, preservatives and trans fats in food, particularly from repeatedly used frying oil, as concerns requiring stronger regulation. Daniel further recommended accessible spaces for physical activity in workplaces, including walkways, trees and encouragement for workers to use stairs where appropriate. She said access to affordable medicines and wider coverage of the National Health Insurance Scheme was equally important in preventing and managing cardiovascular diseases. On the consequences of excessive working hours, she warned that sleep deprivation and prolonged shifts could expose doctors to additional health risks. Earlier, Chairman of MDCAN, FMC Ebute-Metta, Dr Lucky Okpetu, said the theme was chosen because physicians frequently advise patients to adopt healthy lifestyles but fail to practise the same advice themselves. “We found out that physicians hardly take care of themselves. They themselves don’t look after their hearts. They indulge in things they are not supposed to. They advise their patients to do the right thing. But they do not do what they tell the patients to do,” he said. Okpetu, a consultant haematologist, urged doctors to have personal physicians and undergo regular medical examinations. “The ideal thing to do is, as a physician, you must have your own physician. You have to see your physician regularly,” he said. He listed kidney function, blood sugar and other necessary medical tests among the routine checks doctors should undertake, adding that lifestyle choices remained critical to cardiovascular health. Speaking, the Medical Director and Chief Executive Officer of FMC Ebute-Metta, Dr Saheed Ogunme, also challenged physicians to make patients’ health and well-being their foremost consideration while strengthening collaboration between hospital management and consultants. He stressed that healthcare delivery was a collective responsibility and that no single professional could claim credit for successful patient outcomes. “If a patient comes to our hospital, has a successful surgery and goes home, it’s not the doctor or consultant that has done this alone. It’s the other people too, who participate in the care of that patient,” he said. Ogunme also urged doctors to pay attention to their own health, noting that physicians often have no personal doctors to consult when they become ill. The conference also examined the role of artificial intelligence in reducing workload and addressing manpower shortages in the health sector. Also, Professor of Medicine and Chairman, Medical Advisory Committee, FMC Ebute-Metta, Prof. Adebowale Adekoya, said AI could help reduce burnout by automating routine documentation and administrative tasks. He cited ambient scribe technology, which can listen to conversations between healthcare professionals and patients and convert them into clinical documentation. “AI can listen to conversation between the doctor, the nurse, and their patients. And then transcribe that using voice-to-text, using language models,” he said. However, Adekoya warned that doctors must verify AI-generated information before using it in patient care. “Although the responsibility of making sure that it’s accurate still lies with the caregiver of reading it before posting it,” he said. He also cautioned against applying AI tools developed using foreign population data indiscriminately to Nigerian patients, insisting that local data must inform medical technologies used in the country. “The responsibility is on us now to generate our own data,” he said. Chairman of the occasion, Prof. Oluwatoyin Ashiru, urged medical professionals to protect their physical and emotional well-being, warning that exhausted and distressed doctors could struggle to provide the quality of care expected of them. He challenged professional associations to protect the welfare of healthcare workers, strengthen institutional partnerships and ensure that professional disagreements did not undermine patient care. His message was clear: doctors must protect themselves while protecting others. The post Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: How residents killed BEDC staff for disconnecting building over N300k electricity bill
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE management of the BEDC Electricity Plc on Wednesday called on the security agencies and government to ensure that its 38 years old staff identified as Oscar Nduka Eze who was brutally killed while on duty on Monday gets justice. Eze was reportedly stabbed to death around Idumobi Umunede in the Agbor Unit, Delta State after he disconnected a building said to be owing about N300,000 electricity bill. Shortly after he disconnected the building, he was said to have been trailed to a nearby house by some people suspected to have been from previous place he had gone to work when they reportedly pounced on him and stabbed him severally till he died. Addressing journalists at the company’s office, Acting Managing Director of the company, Jonathan Lawani said the killers wanted to conceal their act but unknown to them, the building which they took him to had security camera. He said “Eze went to work on Monday 16th November 2026 for his official duty to earn a legitimate living. However, at about 12 noon of that same day while he was carrying out his official work along the Idumobi by Umunede within the Agbor Business Unit of our operations in Delta State, some hoodlums, some men who claim to be more powerful than God, who has the power to take life, traced him to a house within the same community and they stabbed him with knife until he died on the spot. Caught on CCTV “What they planned did not work. These people had planned to kill him without any evidence. And what they did was to push him into a compound, a very isolated place where he went to carry out another assignment. Unfortunately for them, that house has a CCTV camera and they were all captured directly. “The simple reason for this is that this officer had disconnected their house for non-payment. The only instrument that have been approved by NERC, the Nigeria Electricity Regulatory Commission to ask for payment or to demand payment for those who refuse to pay us for our monthly electricity. I want to put it straight that what the late Oscar did was an approved and official assignment. “The house in question owes us almost three hundred thousand naira and he disconnected them for non-payment and left the place quietly.” Lawani said Eze just got married four months ago after his wife died. He said five persons have been arrested in connection to the incident. “We cannot bring him back but we must ensure that justice is served. We will do everything in line with the law to see that justice is served,” he added. items.title: ‘Have the courage to listen to the debate you started’: Bilawal sticks to his guns after speaking his ‘truth’
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Wednesday maintained that his recent remarks on the country’s political situation were the “truth”, urging government representatives to have the “courage” to listen to his point of view. Speaking in an interview on Hum News programme ‘Faisla Aap Ka’, Bilawal reiterated his stance from his Tuesday’s speech, cautioning against new provinces and calling for a “political reset” so public issues could be addressed. Bilawal emphasised that he spoke in the context of the US-Iran war, which has impacted economies around the world due to rising energy costs. “Elites do not have the idea of what kind of difficulties Pakistanis are facing,” he said, highlighting the need for politicians to set aside their partisan political perspectives and think about how to “fix the system”. The PPP chairman asserted it was his right to provide his perspective on what shape a “reset” should take if someone was suggesting that a reset was needed, indirectly referring to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s July remarks . On the fact that his PPP was part of the ruling coalition, Bilawal contended that this was the exact reason to “listen” to him as he was a “major stakeholder”. “These are not reasons to discount what I am saying […] I am telling you that this is the situation; these are my proposals to rectify it. You may disagree with my suggestions, but at least listen. You should have the courage to listen to the truth.” The Bhutto scion added, “Because I am a stakeholder, I am saying: come to your senses.” He further said, “Now let’s have the debate that you started. […] Have the courage to [continue] the debate that is now ongoing.” Noting that the conversation had not been brought to the Parliament so far, Bilawal said, “You yourself decided to hold this debate in front of businessmen. It was decided on their own that this debate would be held through touts.” The PPP chairman affirmed that Pakistan had not become so weak as a society that there would only be “one-sided debates”. Replying to a question, he remarked that he “spoke too much truth yesterday, which was now hard to digest”. Noting the ongoing “geopolitical atmosphere”, the former foreign minister wondered how many fronts the government wanted to fight on simultaneously, with India as an adversary, a near-war situation with Afghanistan and the fight against terrorism. “The government has been deciding that we will fight the PTI; now the new decision is that they will also fight JUI, and it seems that after my truth, they have also decided they must fight me too,” Bilawal remarked. “If you are going to fight everyone, and fight everyone internally as well, then who will lead Pakistan and its people out of this economic crisis?” he wondered. The PPP chairman said the reactions from federal ministers to his remarks were “yet another proof that Pakistan’s politicians do not have the courage to hear the truth”. “If you or they do not have enough courage or patience to listen to me, then what about the people of Pakistan who have no access to the prime minister, his ministers, or the National Assembly?” ‘Want PM Shehbaz to be strengthened’ Asked about his view if the government insisted on forming provinces, Bilawal said: “I would want to say to the incumbent government that the power of ‘ kun fayakun’ belongs only to Allah Almighty and no one else. “And if anyone is under the misconception that a decision was made, spoken, and thus done, then it will have an impact and consequences on our society, on our federation, on our politics, and on the lives of our people.” On the PPP’s allyship with the PML-N, Bilawal said his party was with the government, keeping the national interest in view. He added, “Otherwise, there is political loss for me in bearing the burden of this government and this system.” At the same time, he affirmed that his party still stood with the government and wanted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to be successful. Clarifying any “misunderstanding” that PML-N might have, Bilawal said the aim of his address yesterday was that PM Shehbaz’s “hands are strengthened”. Asked if he could leave the ruling coalition if he was not heard, the Bhutto scion said, “There is no extraordinary interest in sitting on the treasury benches or opposition benches.” He added that if the government “did not have enough courage to tolerate the well-meaning input of their allies, then I wouldn’t lose any sleep if I was sitting on the opposition benches”. ‘Unaware of what is behind provinces debate’ Bilawal said he was unaware of “what was behind this debate because till today, despite being such a major stakeholder”, neither the prime minister nor a federal minister nor a political or any other stakeholder had discussed with him or the president that they wanted new provinces to be created. “No attention” was being paid to the ongoing historic economic crisis, the ex-minister added. Reiterating that he had not started the debate on governance, Bilawal quipped whether “only the PCB chairman had the right to tell how and why the system has collapsed”, referring to Naqvi, who also serves as the cricket board chief. “If a reset has to happen, then has the PCB been given the responsibility that you have all powers to decide how the system will be reset, whether provinces should be divided? […] Should I go home quietly? This is not possible.” Asked whether his remarks meant that PPP would take the path of resistance, Bilawal refrained from terming it that, adding that he provided his voters’ perspective and did not issue any protest call. “I suggested to everyone that a political reset is needed, a democratic reset is needed, so that instead of politicians grabbing each other’s collars, fighting each other, we all join hands to pull the public out of this hardship,” he explained. The PPP chairman termed the government’s reaction to criticism by Maulana Fazlur Rehman as “completely frivolous, irresponsible conduct”. “If he criticises, the reaction is to demolish the house, arrest his son and pressure his party workers,” he added. Asked whether his warning regarding the division of Sindh was a threat, the Bhutto scion affirmed that his party was not one that engaged in violence. He referred to Sindh’s history, particularly from the 1980s onwards, adding, “Was what I said outside of a historical context or precedent? This wasn’t organic; it was orchestrated to create division in Sindh’s politics.” He declared, “And this risk is still present today, which is why I was warning that if Sindh is divided forcefully, I would not do such things but there will be a reaction.” Bilawal warned that while he would not want it, the law and order situation would worsen so much that it would be difficult to put out the “fire”. ‘Not disowning 27th Amendment’ On him questioning the 27th Amendment , Bilawal stressed that the amendment lacked the same “unanimous consensus” that was present for the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment. He stated that the 26th Amendment was passed with input from the opposition through the JUI-F chief, but it was the 27th Amendment that was followed by resignations of senior judges. He emphasised that he was not calling for withdrawing the amendments, but that the opposition’s input be considered in such legislation. In a separate interview on Geo News , Bilawal clarified he was “not disowning the 27th Amendment”. He elaborated that there was a “difference” in the 18th, 26th and 27th Amendments regarding the consensus each of them had. The PPP chairman declared he was “proud that we formed a constitutional court”, and that it had equal representation from all provinces. Bilawal emphasised that he had presented suggestions on how confidence can be restored not just in the judiciary, but in other institutions as well, including the Parliament and the election commission, if there was to be a “political reset”. “Do I believe the 27th Amendment could be more powerful with more input? Absolutely,” the PPP chief stated, stressing that he still believed judicial reforms were needed so that judges did not interfere in irrelevant matters. “If you don’t want a reset, if you don’t want to improve the situation, then continue things as they are. But it can’t be that only one person is allowed and only one point of view is legitimate and any other is illegitimate.” ‘Reserved seats a low-hanging fruit if political reset pursued’ Speaking on Hum News about his remarks on reserved seats , Bilawal termed it a “low-hanging fruit if there was to be a political reset and if the opposition’s confidence was to be restored”. “If we are to have a political reset, if we are to work towards a system that solves the economic issues of the people of Pakistan, one of the low-hanging fruits to improve the confidence of the opposition to convince them to start trusting Parliament in the political system is this suggestion — not this direction, not this insistence or red line.” Asked about how such a process could begin as it would alter the coalition’s strength in the Parliament, Bilawal replied it could only happen if everyone agreed. “If the government says no, we do not want to do so, then I cannot force anything,” said the PPP chairman about their ally PML-N. Responding to a query about reserved seats on Geo News , Bilawal emphasised that his suggestion was “in the context of a political, democratic reset that could restore the trust of the opposition parties”. He remarked that in the case of such a reset, considering giving back PTI its reserved seats “through the courts or legislation could be part of a confidence-building measure”. On the PPP possibly giving up its reserved seats, Bilawal contended that this was “not the legal position as of now”, adding that they would not go to PTI even if his lawmakers resign. “I think there’s an attempt of purpose to sensationalise what I said, to delegitimise and take out of context what I said, to serve some other purpose,” he further said.

items.title: PDP delegation visits injured APC leaders at Gombe hospital
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe In a significant demonstration of political tolerance, sportsmanship and solidarity, the Gombe State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has paid a solidarity visit to leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) who sustained injuries in a road accident while returning from a campaign rally on Tuesday. The PDP delegation, led by the Director-General of its Campaign Council, Hon. Dan’azumi Adamu Pindiga, visited the injured APC leaders at the Federal Teaching Hospital (FTH), Gombe, on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, to express sympathy and wish them a speedy recovery. Those involved in the accident included the APC State Campaign Council Director-General, Hon. Sa’adu Hassan, and the Gombe State APC Chairman, Hon. Dantata Ndus, alongside other party members. Members of the PDP delegation included the party’s State Secretary, Hon. Adamu Abubakar; Hon. Abubakar Walama; Hon. Sani Hassan Dogarai; Hon. Hassan Santana; Hon. Abubakar Bello (Cikasoron Gombe); and Hon. Jalo Ahmed Ganga. During the visit, Pindiga conveyed messages of solidarity and goodwill on behalf of the PDP leader in Gombe State, former Governor, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, OON, PhD, Talban Gombe; the party’s governorship candidate, Professor Isa Ali Pantami; and the entire PDP family in the state. The delegation also offered prayers to Almighty Allah to grant the injured party chieftains and other victims of the accident complete healing, renewed strength and a speedy recovery. Speaking during the visit, the PDP representatives stressed that political differences should not undermine the bonds of brotherhood, humanity and mutual respect among the people of Gombe State. They maintained that, “beyond party affiliations and electoral interests, political actors remain members of one community with shared responsibilities and a common obligation to promote peaceful coexistence”. According to the delegation, “an unfortunate incident involving members of another political party should attract the concern and sympathy of all, irrespective of political leanings”. The visit, coming amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscores the need for political maturity, tolerance and civility among competing parties and their supporters. It also sends a strong message that political competition should be anchored on issues, policies and the contest for public support, rather than hostility, animosity or division. The PDP delegation reiterated its goodwill towards the injured APC leaders and prayed for their full recovery, stressing that humanity must always take precedence over partisan considerations. According to them, “Politics Should Never Come Before Humanity; We Are All Brothers and sisters”. items.title: Electroland announces Black Friday deals with up to 70% discounts, free appliances and GH¢1m in prizes
items.description: Electroland Ghana Limited has announced its ‘No Challenger’ Black Friday promotion, offering customers discounts of between 30 and 70 per cent, free appliances on selected purchases and the opportunity to win shopping vouchers worth up to GH¢1 million. The promotion, which combines multiple offers, is aimed at rewarding customers for their loyalty while making household appliances more affordable ahead of the Christmas festivities. Speaking to journalists, the National Sales Manager of Electroland Ghana, Vincent Azan-Gbiok, described the campaign as unprecedented, saying it was the first time the company had combined three or four promotional offers into one Black Friday package. He said customers purchasing selected large appliances, including side-by-side refrigerators, would receive another refrigerator free of charge. Similar offers would apply to selected small appliances, allowing customers who purchase items such as irons to receive an additional one at no cost. Mr Azan-Gbiok said the initiative was also intended to help customers acquire gifts for family and friends during the festive season. Beyond the free appliances, customers who purchase any item from Electroland during the promotional period will automatically qualify for a nationwide draw in which 500 lucky winners will receive vouchers worth up to GH¢1 million. He stressed that eligibility would not depend on the amount spent, giving every customer who makes a qualifying purchase an opportunity to win. The winners will be selected randomly after the promotion ends, with the exercise covering all Electroland showrooms nationwide. Successful customers will be contacted by telephone and directed to their nearest showroom to receive their prizes. Mr Azan-Gbiok also disclosed that the company’s year-long Akyediɛ Kɛseɛ promotion would continue alongside the Black Friday campaign. Under the scheme, customers are automatically entered into a prize draw whenever they purchase from Electroland. He said some beneficiaries had received gifts worth up to 10 times the value of the products they originally purchased, adding that the company remained committed to honouring its promotional promises. The National Sales Manager further announced that the discounts would cover all items in Electroland’s showrooms, with price reductions ranging from 30 to 70 per cent. He clarified that complimentary items attached to selected purchases would be handed over immediately, while prizes won through the subsequent draws would be communicated to successful customers. The company, he said, had put measures in place to manage the anticipated increase in customer turnout and ensure a comfortable shopping experience across its spacious, air-conditioned showrooms. He, however, appealed to customers to exercise patience should the promotional period attract overwhelming numbers, assuring them that staff would make every effort to provide efficient service. The No Challenger promotion is scheduled to run from November 27 to 29 , while the general Black Friday discounts are expected to be available from November 26 to 29 across Electroland showrooms nationwide.

items.title: Crise climatique: l’Afrique hausse le ton et réclame le respect des engagements financiers
items.description: Réunis à Antalya, en Türkiye, en marge de la Cop31, les ministres africains de l’Environnement ont réaffirmé leurs exigences en matière de justice climatique, de financement et d’adaptation. Ils ont appelé la communauté internationale à traduire les promesses en engagements financiers concrets, à la hauteur des défis du continent. ANTALYA – La Conférence ministérielle africaine sur l’environnement (Amcen) s’est réunie à Antalya, en Türkiye, en marge de la Conférence des Nations unies sur les changements climatiques (Cop31). Cette réunion ministérielle de haut niveau s’est tenue en amont d’une étape importante pour la gouvernance environnementale africaine : la vingt-et-unième session ordinaire du Conseil consultatif africain pour l’environnement (Amcen-21) et la cinquante-neuvième Conférence des ministres africains des Finances, de la Planification et du Développement économique (Com2027), prévues en mars 2027 à Addis-Abeba, en Éthiopie. La rencontre a été axée sur les priorités de l’Afrique dans les négociations de la Cop31 et les préparatifs de la Cop32 en Éthiopie. Les discussions ont notamment porté sur le financement climatique, l’adaptation, la transition juste et les changements climatiques. Le ministre sénégalais de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique a fait entendre la voix de l’Afrique. « La justice climatique et la question des responsabilités historiques et différenciées doivent gouverner nos positions. Bien que notre contribution aux émissions mondiales de gaz à effet de serre soit minime, nous subissons les impacts les plus sévères de la crise climatique », a déploré Aliou Gori Diouf. Selon le chef de la délégation sénégalaise, le financement climatique est bien plus qu’un outil économique : il est le symbole de la solidarité internationale et d’un engagement collectif à construire un avenir durable. « Vous êtes conscients de notre vulnérabilité et de notre potentiel en matière d’opportunités pour faire face aux changements climatiques. L’Afrique peut être un continent de solutions, avec l’appui adéquat et équitable de la communauté internationale », a fait savoir le ministre sénégalais de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique. Arlette Soudan-Nonault, ministre congolaise de l’Environnement, du Bassin du Congo et du Développement durable, a, de son côté, rappelé le potentiel que représente le bassin du Congo, avec ses 1,5 milliard de tonnes de carbone séquestrées et ses 30 milliards de tonnes stockées dans ses tourbières. « Nous parlons beaucoup de forêts, mais nous oublions souvent cet écosystème qui fait la différence. Sans les tourbières du bassin du Congo, nous ne pouvons pas maintenir la température de la planète à 1,5 °C », a-t-elle averti. Pour Dre Zanetor Agyemam-Rawlings, ministre ghanéenne de l’Environnement, des Sciences, des Technologies et de l’Innovation, l’Afrique ne représente que 4% des émissions mondiales, mais subit davantage les conséquences des changements climatiques. « Ce qui se passe, c’est une injustice. Personne ne nous fait de faveur. L’Afrique ne renégocie pas des promesses », a-t-elle lancé à l’endroit de la communauté internationale. Selon elle, les parties se sont mises d’accord pour tripler le financement climatique d’ici à 2030, mais la lacune majeure réside dans le non-respect de ces engagements. « Antalya doit se mettre d’accord sur l’évaluation des besoins. Les pertes et préjudices ne sont pas une charité. Nous avons des plans clairs ; le seul problème, c’est que les promesses ne sont pas respectées », a dénoncé la fille de l’ancien président ghanéen, Jerry Rawlings. Nd. M. SECK (Envoyé spécial)

items.title: ONP : hausse de 27% des débarquements de pêche au port de Larache
items.description: L’Office national des pêches (ONP), a fait état d’une hausse de 27% des débarquements des produits de la pêche côtière et artisanale au port de Larache à fin octobre 2026, pour s’établir à 14.747 tonnes (T). Dans son dernier rapport sur les statistiques de la pêche côtière et artisanale au Maroc, l'Office précise que la valeur marchande de ces captures a stagné à 265,94 millions de dirhams (MDH), contre 266 MDH à fin octobre 2025. Par espèce, les quantités de poissons pélagiques débarquées dans ce port ont augmenté de 31% à fin octobre dernier à 11.984 T, pour une valeur estimée à 77,47 MDH, contre plus de 71,83 MDH/ 9.139 T soit +8% en glissement annuel. Les débarquements des poissons blancs ont, quant à eux, progressé de 36% à 794 T, pour une valeur de plus de 38,6 MDH, contre environ 35,59 MDH (+8%). Concernant les débarquement des céphalopodes, ils ont reculé de 1% à 981 T pour des recettes d'environ 95,79 MDH (-10%), tandis que pour les crustacés, les débarquements ont augmenté de 8% à 986 T, générant des revenus de plus de 54,08 MDH (+4%). Au niveau national, les débarquements des produits commercialisés de la pêche côtière et artisanale se sont établis à plus de 1,2 million de tonnes à fin octobre dernier, en hausse de 27% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. En valeur, ces débarquements ont augmenté de 9% à près de 9,77 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) contre plus de 8,94 MMDH en glissement annuel. The post ONP : hausse de 27% des débarquements de pêche au port de Larache appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Aliou Gori Diouf au sommet de la Cop31: « L’Afrique ne veut plus répondre aux transitions qui lui sont imposées »
items.description: Au sommet des dirigeants de la Cop31 à Antalya (en Türkiye), le ministre de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique, Aliou Gori Diouf, a plaidé, hier, pour une transition climatique conçue selon les réalités africaines. Il a notamment appelé à des financements prévisibles pour l’adaptation, la transition énergétique et les marchés carbone, dénonçant les promesses internationales qui tardent à se concrétiser. ANTALAYA – Le ministre de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique a parlé hier sans langue de bois à l’occasion du sommet des dirigeants de la trente-et-unième session de la Conférence des Parties (Cop31) à la Convention-cadre des Nations unies sur les changements climatiques. D’emblée, Aliou Gori Diouf a insisté sur la nécessité de dépasser le simple constat des bouleversements climatiques pour privilégier une action collective fondée sur les réalités de chaque pays. « Nous allons quitter Antalya avec, pour nous en féliciter, un premium stratégique. Il s’agit de reconnaître que l’intelligence collective constitue un atout pour la survie de notre planète. Nous voyons tous que le climat change, mais le constat suffit-il ? », s’est-il interrogé. Pour le ministre, oui, il faut négocier, mais cela ne veut pas dire que les pays qui subissent viennent pour quémander. Si les principes de l’action climatique peuvent être communs, leur mise en œuvre doit, selon lui, tenir compte des réalités propres à chaque territoire. « Soyons capables de mesurer ensemble, de comprendre ensemble et d’agir selon nos réalités. L’Afrique ne veut plus répondre aux transitions qui lui sont imposées ; elle veut les façonner », a-t-il soutenu. Aliou Gori Diouf estime ainsi que « s’adapter, c’est refuser la fatalité et choisir de tenir debout : bâtir des systèmes de production et des écosystèmes résilients, protéger nos communautés et leurs moyens d’existence, et préserver l’avenir de nos enfants ». Il a relevé que face à cette urgence, le Sénégal, pays sahélien, qui affronte les inondations annuelles, la sécheresse, l’érosion côtière, la montée du niveau de la mer et la dégradation de ses bases productives, porte trois priorités. La première, souligne le ministre de l’Environnement, c’est le financement de l’adaptation et les pertes et dommages. « Le triplement du financement de l’adaptation doit cesser d’être une promesse. Ce financement relève de la justice climatique et ne doit pas alourdir la dette des pays vulnérables », a-t-il fait savoir. La deuxième priorité du Sénégal, c’est l’obtention de financements prévisibles pour la transition énergétique et les Contributions déterminées sur le plan national (Cdn). « Dans notre sous-région, l’Afrique de l’Ouest, près de 60% de la population n’a pas accès à l’électricité. Au Sénégal, les énergies renouvelables atteignent déjà 27% de la puissance électrique, vers l’objectif de 40% en 2030 », a-t-il mentionné. Le ministre de l’Environnement note que cet engagement pour les énergies renouvelables renforce les efforts du Sénégal sur les technologies les plus sobres en carbone. « Notre Cdn 3.0 est validée, cependant, sans financements prévisibles et accessibles, ses cibles resteront hors de portée », a-t-il indiqué. La troisième priorité du Sénégal, ce sont des marchés carbones intègres, « véritable levier de financement pour l’Afrique ». Énergies renouvelables À travers cette orientation, Dakar veut promouvoir des mécanismes susceptibles de mobiliser des ressources supplémentaires pour accompagner les efforts du continent en matière de lutte contre le changement climatique. Mais au-delà de ces trois priorités, c’est surtout la question de l’efficacité et de la rapidité des engagements financiers qui demeure au cœur du plaidoyer sénégalais. Le ministre de l’Environnement a ainsi interpellé les partenaires internationaux sur le décalage persistant entre les promesses formulées dans les conférences climatiques et leur concrétisation auprès des populations. « Nous quittons Antalya avec une seule question : combien de temps faudra-t-il pour que le financement de l’adaptation arrive sur le terrain, auprès des communautés qui se lassent des promesses non tenues ? », a-t-il lancé. Une interpellation qui résume, à ses yeux, l'exigence de justice climatique portée par les pays les plus exposés. « On ne peut pas demander à un pays qui se noie de s’endetter pour payer les inondations provoquées par d’autres », a-t-il martelé. Pour Aliou Gori Diouf, Antalya doit ainsi tenir la promesse d’une solidarité climatique devenue réalité. Car, comme il l’a rappelé en conclusion : « L’histoire ne retiendra pas nos discours : elle jugera nos décisions. » De notre envoyé spécial en Türkiye, Ndiol Maka SECK

items.title: US strategist restricts X comments after Tinubu interview backlash
items.description: An American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has restricted access to the comment section of her X account following criticism from Nigerian users over her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu. London interviewed Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday and was subsequently photographed with the President and his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila. Following the interview, she published several posts on X expressing support for the Nigerian government’s security cooperation with the United States. In one of the posts, London described the US-Nigeria security partnership as one that was “delivering results”, crediting Tinubu and US President Donald Trump for their commitment to tackling terrorism. “The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace through strength. None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government,” she wrote. She also described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, expressing optimism that the relationship could create additional economic and trade opportunities for both countries. In another post, London expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria, particularly on initiatives relating to the protection of religious groups and strengthening relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government. However, the posts were subsequently deleted from her X account amid criticism from Nigerian social media users over her engagement with the Tinubu administration. The controversy followed a report by Peoples Gazette alleging that London received $4.5 million for the interview assignment. The allegation generated reactions on social media, with some users questioning the reported payment and the nature of the engagement. Checks on her X account on Wednesday showed that access to the comment section had been restricted, with a notice indicating that only selected accounts could respond to her posts. Before the restriction, some users had questioned her decision to delete the posts praising the Nigerian government’s security partnership with the United States. London had not publicly explained the deletion of the posts or the restriction of comments as of the time of filing this report. The post US strategist restricts X comments after Tinubu interview backlash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Oforikrom assembly empowers 43 PWDs with start-up kits, settles hospital bills to curb street begging
items.description: The Oforikrom Municipal Assembly in the Ashanti Region has provided start-up kits and financial support to settle the medical bills of forty-three (43) Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) in the municipality. The support is part of efforts aimed at improving the livelihoods of the differently-abled persons and discouraging street begging. The intervention, facilitated by the assembly’s Social Welfare Department, was funded through the quarterly allocation of the District Assemblies Common Fund allocated to Persons with Disabilities. The items presented included deep freezers, catering equipment, provisions, bags of charcoal and other business start-up kits to enable beneficiaries to establish and expand their businesses. Other beneficiaries also had their outstanding medical bills in various hospitals settled. Presenting the items at a ceremony in Oforikrom, the Municipal Chief Executive, Ahmed Anwal Sadat, said the exercise marked the fourth disbursement of the PWD fund under his administration. He noted that the proper utilisation of the fund was gradually improving the living conditions of persons with disabilities, many of whom previously depended on street begging for survival. “Initially, most persons with disabilities were on the streets begging, but through the proper use of the PWD fund, we are gradually getting them off the streets. By the end of our four-year term, the majority of PWDs in the Oforikrom Municipality will no longer depend on street begging,” he said. According to him, the assembly, through its Social Welfare Department, monitors beneficiaries to ensure the start-up kits are harnessed for their intended purposes. Mr. Sadat further assured that the assembly would ensure the timely disbursement of the five percent PWD fund disbursed quarterly, stressing that the current administration is committed to clearing outstanding arrears. “We will ensure that the five per cent PWD fund received every quarter is disbursed to persons with disabilities in the municipality. We will not keep the money as was done under some previous administrations. We have now been able to settle all outstanding backlogs,” he stated. Municipal Social Welfare Director, Mary Serwaa Adjen, said the items were selected based on the specific needs and requests of the beneficiaries to ensure they served their intended purposes. “They selected the items they needed, and we purchased them accordingly. We did not decide for them,” she explained. She encouraged other persons with disabilities who had not benefited from the intervention to register with the department to enable them to access similar support in subsequent distributions. Mrs. Adjen, however, cautioned beneficiaries against misusing the items, warning that the assembly would retrieve any equipment not used for its intended purpose and reallocate it to another deserving person. The 43 persons with disabilities who benefited from the latest disbursement represent an increase in the number of beneficiaries, attributable to the rise in the PWD fund allocation – from three to five per cent. Some of the beneficiaries expressed gratitude to the Oforikrom assembly and the government for the support, emphasizing that the start-up kits would help improve their livelihoods and promote their economic independence.

items.title: L’Institut Pasteur de Dakar au cœur de la souveraineté sanitaire
items.description: L’Institut Pasteur de Dakar a ouvert, hier, la quatrième édition du Dakar Epidemics Forum. Durant trois jours, les échanges portent sur la surveillance épidémiologique, le diagnostic, la recherche et la production locale de vaccins et de produits de santé. À l’ouverture des travaux, de l’édition du Dakar Epidemics Forum, Dr Ibrahima Socé Fall, administrateur général de l’Institut Pasteur de Dakar, a rappelé la fréquence des alertes épidémiques dans la région africaine de l’Organisation mondiale de la Santé (Oms). Selon les chiffres présentés, le continent enregistre entre 120 et 150 épidémies par an. Cette situation appelle un renforcement des dispositifs de surveillance et des capacités de réponse des pays. L’Institut Pasteur de Dakar entend apporter sa contribution à cet effort à travers ses activités de recherche, de diagnostic et de production. Parmi les avancées mises en avant figure la reprise de la production du vaccin contre la fièvre jaune, après plusieurs années d’interruption. L’institution travaille également au développement de solutions diagnostiques adaptées aux besoins des systèmes de santé africains. Un test rapide de diagnostic de la rougeole a été évoqué au cours de la cérémonie. L’Ipd poursuit par ailleurs le développement de ses plateformes de recherche et de formation. Pour son administrateur général, les compétences développées sur le continent doivent aussi pouvoir bénéficier à d’autres régions du monde. « Pour la première fois, nous voyons une demande pour le transfert de technologie de l’Afrique vers les autres continents », a souligné Dr Fall. La surveillance des épidémies ne repose pas uniquement sur les laboratoires et les structures spécialisées. Les communautés jouent également un rôle important dans le repérage des premiers signes d’une maladie inhabituelle. Les chefs de village, les agents de santé des structures éloignées et les familles peuvent contribuer à faire remonter rapidement les alertes. C’est l’un des points développés par Elhadj As Sy, président du Conseil de Fondation de l’Institut Pasteur de Dakar. Il a insisté sur la nécessité d’associer les populations aux dispositifs de prévention et de riposte. La confiance entre les communautés et les institutions sanitaires constitue, selon lui, une condition importante pour l’efficacité des interventions. Le représentant résident de l’Oms, N’da Konan Michel Yao, a indiqué à son tour que les épidémies se développent dans un contexte marqué par les conflits, les déplacements de populations, l’insécurité alimentaire et les crises climatiques. Il a appelé les États africains à investir davantage dans la surveillance, les laboratoires, la recherche et la production locale afin de réduire leur dépendance aux chaînes d’approvisionnement internationales. Au Sénégal, le renforcement des capacités de préparation et de riposte figure parmi les priorités présentées par le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, Dr Ibrahima Sy. Ce dernier a insisté sur la nécessité de détecter rapidement les menaces, de confirmer les alertes et d’organiser sans délai la réponse sanitaire. Le ministre a également annoncé que le projet de budget 2027 de son département prévoit plus de 6 milliards de francs Cfa pour l’acquisition de vaccins destinés au Programme élargi de vaccination. Il a fait état d’un financement de près de 14 milliards de francs Cfa sur trois ans, mobilisé dans le cadre du Pandemic Fund pour soutenir la surveillance épidémiologique, les laboratoires et les ressources humaines. Le Sénégal ambitionne par ailleurs de couvrir 50% de ses besoins en vaccins et médicaments d’ici à 2035. À l’échelle continentale, l’Union africaine vise la production locale de 60% des vaccins nécessaires à l’Afrique à l’horizon 2040. « La sécurité sanitaire ne commence pas à la première alerte. Elle se construit bien avant », a déclaré Ibrahima Sy. Amadou Kébé

items.title: Government committed to building a competitive economy, supporting local businesses – Julius Debrah
items.description: Chief of Staff Julius Debrah has reaffirmed the government’s commitment to building a productive, competitive and resilient economy that creates jobs, supports local businesses and improves the living conditions of Ghanaians. He said the government was focused on creating an enabling environment for businesses to invest, expand and compete in the global market. “As a government, our focus is clear: to build a productive, competitive and resilient economy that creates jobs, expands local industries and improves livelihoods,” he said. Dr Debrah highlighted four key initiatives underpinning the government’s economic agenda: the New Economy Programme, the 24-Hour Economy, the Accelerated Export Development Programme and the Big Push Infrastructure Programme. “Through the New Economy Programme, the 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme, and the Big Push Infrastructure Programme, we are creating the conditions for businesses to invest, grow and compete globally,” Dr Debrah added. He was speaking at the closing ceremony of the maiden Invest Ghana Summit 2026, which brought together investors, business leaders, development partners and other stakeholders for discussions on Ghana’s investment opportunities and economic potential. The Chief of Staff said the two-day summit had provided an important platform for discussions on investment opportunities across various sectors and engagements with prospective investors on turning business interests into actual projects. He also expressed satisfaction with activities at the Deal Room and Investor Facilitation Hub, where Ghanaian businesses, international investors and financial institutions explored opportunities for partnerships and collaboration. Dr Debrah stressed that the priority now was to ensure that discussions and engagements at the summit translated into actual investments, business expansion and decent employment opportunities. “Our task now is to sustain these conversations and ensure they translate into investments, enterprises and dignified employment opportunities for our people,” he said. He commended Mr Simon Madjie and his team at the Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC), together with the summit’s partners and stakeholders, for their contributions towards the success of the maiden edition. He further urged international investors and business representatives to take advantage of the opportunities Ghana offers by moving beyond discussions to establish meaningful partnerships and deliver tangible results. “Ghana is ready for business. Let us move beyond conversations to partnerships and from opportunities to measurable results,” Dr Debrah said. He reiterated the government’s commitment to supporting investments that drive economic growth and create opportunities for Ghanaians.

items.title: Cambodia’s Repression Hangs Over Francophonie Summit
items.description: Click to expand Image French President Emmanuel Macron (left) with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet during the 20th Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh, November 15, 2026. © 2026 Chalinee Thirasupa/Reuters As world leaders recently gathered in Phnom Penh to celebrate the 20th Francophonie Summit with the theme of peace and shared prosperity, French President Emmanuel Macron took to the podium to call publicly for an investigation into the killing of former Cambodian lawmaker and French citizen Lim Kimya. It was a rare public rebuke of the Cambodian government by a foreign leader. A gunman killed Kimya in Bangkok, Thailand in January 2025. Kimya had served as a parliament member with the opposition Cambodia National Rescue Party before its 2017 dissolution. A Thai court convicted the gunman, Ekkalak Paenoi, in October 2025 and issued arrest warrants for two Cambodian suspects, Ly Ratanakraksmey and Pich Kimsrin, both of whom have connections to high-ranking Cambodian officials. The Cambodian government—like many of its neighbors in Southeast Asia—is increasingly persecuting activists abroad. The Cambodian government has yet to acknowledge the arrest warrants or start an impartial investigation. Both men remain at large. France has issued Interpol Red Notices for them on charges of complicity in premeditated murder. Macron’s raising Kimya’s murder during a joint press conference with Prime Minister Hun Manet sends a strong message that the French government is taking Cambodian authorities’ attacks on activists abroad seriously. The Cambodian government should heed the call and independently and impartially investigate the murder. But political repression by the Cambodian government runs deeper than one case. Ahead of 2027 local elections, the authorities are escalating their crackdown on the long suppressed political opposition. Young activists in particular, such as the five imprisoned Mother Nature Cambodia environmental activists, have been punished with baseless treason charges and lengthy prison sentences. Concerned governments should publicly and privately urge Cambodian authorities to release the more than 100 Cambodians currently imprisoned for exercising their fundamental freedoms. Human Rights Watch was among the local and international organizations that pressed Cambodian authorities to release the Mother Nature activists and others ahead of the Francophonie Summit. The ruling Cambodian People’s Party, which exerts complete control over the country’s courts, was apparently unbothered by these efforts. Other foreign leaders should amplify Macron’s message and publicly call on Cambodia’s government to reopen the space for the political opposition and respect the fundamental rights of all Cambodians, both at home and abroad.

items.title: Gov’t considers PPP to build affordable hostels for tertiary students – Education Minister reveals
items.description: Government is considering a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement to facilitate the construction of additional hostel facilities at affordable rates for tertiary students. Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu disclosed this after engaging the Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, and the Director-General of the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC), Professor Ahmed Jinapor, over concerns about rising hostel accommodation fees. The proposed partnership is expected to help address the growing demand for student accommodation while easing the financial burden on students. At the meeting, Mr Iddrisu acknowledged the challenges associated with the increasing demand for hostel facilities but stressed the need to balance the interests of students, hostel operators and tertiary institutions. He also directed GTEC to collaborate with the Rent Control Commission to explore measures to regulate hostel accommodation costs and prevent students from being disadvantaged by escalating rental charges. The engagement followed an appeal by the Acting Rent Commissioner for the Education Minister’s intervention in what he described as excessive cost of hostel accommodation.

items.title: 2026 harvest reduces food prices, says Kyari
items.description: …Niger leads rice, yam production — NAERLS report By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has said increased food production during the 2026 wet season has contributed to a reduction in food prices despite persistent challenges in the agricultural sector. Kyari spoke on Wednesday during the presentation of the 2026 Agricultural Performance Survey Report by the Executive Director of the National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services (NAERLS), Professor Yusuf Sani, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. The minister said the report indicated an increase in agricultural output compared with 2025, attributing the development to government interventions aimed at boosting food production and improving affordability. He cited reductions in the prices of commodities such as garri and millet, saying the trend reflected improvements in food supply. “When you do comparison between 2025 and 2026, I am not even comparing 2023 and 2026, just within the one year, we have seen prices dropping — garri, millet, and so on and so forth, that has come down,” he said. Kyari added that another harvest was expected within the next month, which he said could further improve food availability. On agricultural mechanisation, he said deliveries under the second phase of the programme were expected within the next two to three months. He also disclosed that the Federal Government planned to release food commodities stored under the Guaranteed Minimum Price (GMP) programme through the Bank of Agriculture to help stabilise market prices. “That is also in the works, and very soon we will announce how the methodology of that release will be made,” he said. On fertiliser supply, Kyari said the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative planned to release three million bags of fertiliser within one month to reduce input costs for farmers. He said the programme, announced by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, was part of efforts to improve agricultural productivity and balance the interests of farmers, processors and consumers. The minister also pointed to increased private-sector investment in agricultural processing, particularly in cocoa, sesame, soybean and shea nut. He said investments by multinational companies in the country’s agricultural sector indicated growing confidence in Nigeria’s business environment. Kyari further disclosed that $33 million had been invested in the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ) programme. He said government interventions over the past three years had contributed to increased productivity across several crop categories, although some crops continued to record declines. Presenting the survey findings, NAERLS Executive Director, Professor Yusuf Sani, said Niger State emerged as the country’s leading producer of rice and yam. He said Ogun State ranked second in rice production, although its rice yield per hectare was lower than that of Niger State. Sani attributed Niger State’s performance partly to the adoption of improved farming practices by farmers, noting the presence of the National Cereals Research Institute in Badeggi. For yam production, he said Niger State also ranked first, with Akwa Ibom among the 10 leading producing states. Kano State emerged as the leading onion producer, followed by Kebbi and Sokoto, while Taraba also featured among the top 10 states. On national agricultural output, Sani said cereal production increased by 1.8 per cent compared with 2025, reaching approximately 29.4 million metric tonnes. He disclosed that 13 of the 17 major crops assessed recorded higher production during the period, while ginger, cocoyam, millet and soybean recorded declines. The survey also identified limited access to quality seeds as the leading constraint affecting farmers, accounting for 28.8 per cent of reported production challenges. Other constraints included inadequate agricultural extension services and training, family and labour-related challenges, and insufficient access to grants and farm inputs. Sani also identified ginger blight as one of the factors affecting farmers’ output. On regional agricultural performance, he said the North-Central zone led production of cereals, legumes, roots and tubers, while the North-West accounted for the largest share of vegetable production at about 31 per cent. The post 2026 harvest reduces food prices, says Kyari appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana secures 6.57 million forest carbon credits, becomes first African country to receive ART TREES credits
items.description: Ghana has received 6.57 million carbon credits for reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, with the government expecting about US$43 million from the sale of some of the credits. The credits were issued to the Government of Ghana on November 12, 2026, under the Architecture for REDD+ Transactions (ART), making the country the first in Africa to receive credits under the programme. They cover forest protection efforts across approximately 2.5 million hectares between 2017 and 2021. Ghana is also the first country to receive credits under ART’s TREES Crediting Level approach with the Core Carbon Principles (CCP) Approved label from the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market (ICVCM). The issuance follows years of work to improve forest monitoring and reduce the activities responsible for forest loss. It also gives Ghana an opportunity to raise funds for forest protection and support farmers and communities whose livelihoods depend on forest resources. The 6.57 million credits recognise reductions in greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation and forest degradation under Ghana’s REDD+ programme. REDD+ stands for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation. It also covers forest conservation, sustainable forest management and efforts to increase carbon stored in forests. Agricultural expansion, illegal mining and logging have put pressure on Ghana’s forests. Cocoa production has also contributed to forest loss in some areas as farms expand into forest landscapes. Ghana’s programme brings together government agencies, cocoa farmers, private companies and local communities to address these pressures while supporting more sustainable agricultural practices. To qualify for the credits, Ghana had to provide evidence of its emissions reductions using systems that measure changes in forest cover and estimate the amount of carbon released or removed. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has supported the Forestry Commission in improving the country’s forest monitoring, measurement and reporting systems. The support included the use of digital tools to collect and analyse forest information, helping Ghana prepare the documents required under the TREES standard. According to FAO, Ghana submitted 11.9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) in emissions reductions for the 2017–2021 period. About 90 per cent of the reported reductions came from lower emissions associated with deforestation and forest degradation, while the remaining 10 per cent resulted from increased carbon removals through forest restoration. However, ART issued 6.57 million credits following the assessment and verification process. The two figures represent different stages of the crediting process. The 11.9 million tonnes were reported by Ghana, while the 6.57 million credits are the volume officially issued under the programme. The public announcement does not provide a full explanation of the difference. This distinction is important because reported emissions reductions do not automatically become carbon credits. They must meet the requirements of the applicable standard and undergo the necessary assessment before issuance. What the CCP Approved label means Ghana’s credits have received the Core Carbon Principles Approved label, a quality mark developed by the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market. The principles set requirements for carbon credits traded in the voluntary market. They cover how emissions reductions are measured, independent verification, transparent tracking, effective governance and the protection of people and the environment. ART’s TREES Crediting Level approach received CCP approval in 2024. Ghana’s issuance is the first batch of TREES credits to carry the label. With the latest issuance , Ghana has also become the third country in the world to receive TREES credits under ART, after Guyana and Costa Rica. Guyana received credits under ART’s High Forest, Low Deforestation approach, while Costa Rica received credits under its Removals approach, which recognises forest restoration. The approval could make the credits more attractive to companies looking to buy carbon credits that meet recognised quality requirements. However, the label does not mean the credits have been sold or that Ghana has received payment. It is also different from approval under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement or eligibility under the aviation industry’s CORSIA offsetting programme, which have separate requirements. The government expects to receive about US$43 million from the initial sale of some of the newly issued credits. At COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, said the expected payments were linked to the anticipated purchase of about four million tonnes of emissions reductions. The proposed prices range from US$10 to US$13 per tonne. “Ghana is proud to lead the way as the first African country to access climate finance through the LEAF Coalition. This is a landmark achievement that recognises the dedication of our communities, farmers and government to protecting Ghana’s forests while pursuing sustainable development. This finance will support our communities in advancing agroforestry, improving livelihoods, and demonstrating that economic growth and forest conservation can go hand in hand,” he said. The LEAF Coalition is among the buyers associated with Ghana’s forest carbon programme. The coalition brings together governments and private companies seeking to finance the protection of tropical and subtropical forests through the purchase of verified emissions reductions. Ghana’s involvement in the LEAF Coalition dates back to COP28 in December 2023, when it became the first country in the world to sign a binding Emissions Reductions Purchase Agreement under the coalition. The agreement, signed with Emergent , the organisation coordinating the coalition, provided for the potential purchase of up to five million tonnes of emissions reductions, valued at up to US$50 million. The expected US$43 million is not confirmed revenue already received by Ghana. The relevant transactions and payment arrangements must be completed before the country receives the money. The anticipated purchase of four million tonnes would also leave some of the 6.57 million issued credits outside the initial transaction. How farmers and communities could benefit The distribution of the expected revenue will be important, particularly for farmers and communities whose activities and livelihoods are closely linked to forest areas. Ghana’s Cocoa Forest REDD+ Programme includes arrangements for sharing emissions reduction payments with farmer groups and local communities. Under Ghana’s Cocoa Forest REDD+ Programme , 69 per cent of emissions-reduction payments are allocated to local stakeholders in designated intervention areas. The share is divided among farmer groups, traditional authorities and local communities. The benefit-sharing plan is intended to reward those involved in reducing deforestation and improving forest management. Separately, the LEAF Coalition’s transaction arrangements provide for more than two-thirds of net proceeds to go to local stakeholders through an agreed benefit-sharing process. These are distinct benefit-sharing arrangements, although both place emphasis on directing carbon revenue. Daniel Amponsah, a farmer and Chairman of the Asunafo-Asutifi Hotspot Intervention Area (HIA) Management Board, said the funding could support agroforestry and improve access to essential community services. “This is a gamechanger. LEAF funding will help communities advance sustainable agroforestry, planting shade trees that not only restore forests but also help improve cocoa yields and incomes. And finance from LEAF will also support communities to build new boreholes for fresh water, schools and health facilities,” he said.
