items.title: Autoroute Dakar-Tivaouane-Saint-Louis : Pambal alerte sur les risques d’enclavement
items.description: Des habitants de la commune de Pambal se sont rassemblés, mercredi 18 novembre, à la place publique du village de Kadane pour faire part de leurs préoccupations concernant les aménagements prévus dans le cadre de l'autoroute Dakar-Tivaouane-Saint-Louis (DTS). Le collectif de défense des intérêts de Pambal réclame notamment des passages inférieurs, un échangeur et la clarification de la situation foncière liée au titre minier TF/8M. Il demande également la suspension des travaux de clôture en attendant des réponses à ses revendications. « L'autoroute pour le développement du Sénégal, oui ! L'autoroute qui appauvrit Pambal, non ! » C'est autour de ce slogan que des jeunes, des femmes, des adultes et des personnes âgées se sont retrouvés à Kadane. Arborant des bandeaux et des foulards rouges, les manifestants ont voulu attirer l'attention sur les conséquences que pourrait avoir le tracé de l'infrastructure sur les activités économiques et les déplacements des populations de la commune. Initialement prévue sous forme de marche, la mobilisation s'est finalement limitée à une déclaration devant la presse, les organisateurs ayant été informés de l'interdiction de leur manifestation. À cette occasion, Samba Tine, membre de la commission technique du collectif, a rappelé les différentes démarches entreprises depuis près de six mois pour obtenir des réponses aux préoccupations soulevées. Courriers, mémorandums, lettres ouvertes et rencontres avec les acteurs concernés auraient, selon lui, été multipliés sans aboutir aux résultats attendus. Au cœur des revendications figure d'abord le respect des engagements pris dans le cadre de la réalisation de l'autoroute. Le collectif demande notamment une indemnisation des personnes affectées sur la base du coût intégral de remplacement de leurs biens. Il plaide également pour la construction de passages inférieurs afin de préserver l'accès aux terres agricoles, aux pâturages, aux points d'eau et aux établissements scolaires. « Nous sommes un peuple d'agriculteurs et d'éleveurs. Les passages supérieurs, nous n'en voulons pas ! », a insisté Samba Tine. Sur les pancartes brandies par les manifestants, plusieurs messages mettaient en avant les difficultés redoutées par les élèves et les femmes, notamment en matière de mobilité et d'accès aux services de proximité. Le collectif réclame, par ailleurs, la réalisation d'un échangeur permettant l'entrée et la sortie de l'autoroute au niveau de la commune. Selon ses responsables, cet aménagement figurait dans la conception initiale du projet. Son rétablissement permettrait, à leurs yeux, de mieux intégrer Pambal dans le réseau autoroutier et de favoriser les retombées économiques de l'infrastructure. La question foncière constitue un autre point de préoccupation. Les membres du collectif demandent la levée du titre minier TF/8M, qu'ils estiment contraignant pour le développement de la commune et l'exploitation de ses terres. Face à ces différentes préoccupations, les manifestants souhaitent l'ouverture d'un cadre de concertation permettant d'aboutir à des réponses concrètes. Ils demandent notamment la suspension des travaux de clôture de l'autoroute tant que la question des passages inférieurs n'aura pas été définitivement clarifiée. Le collectif a également sollicité l'arbitrage du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, afin de faciliter le règlement de ce différend. Il dit avoir saisi la Banque africaine de développement (BAD), à travers son Mécanisme indépendant de recours, pour signaler des violations présumées de certaines dispositions de sauvegarde opérationnelle liées au projet. Tout en affirmant ne pas appeler à la violence, les responsables du collectif disent attendre des autorités et des structures concernées des réponses à leurs différentes demandes. Ils souhaitent ainsi que la réalisation de l'autoroute puisse s'accompagner d'aménagements garantissant la continuité des activités agricoles, pastorales et sociales dans la commune. Ibrahima NDIAYE (Correspondant)

items.title: Naira weakens to N1,470/$ at parallel market
items.description: The naira depreciated to N1,470 per dollar at the parallel foreign exchange market on Wednesday, its weakest performance since January 28. The latest rate represented a N25, or 1.73 per cent, decline from the N1,445 per dollar quoted on Tuesday. Currency traders, popularly known as Bureau De Change operators, in Lagos quoted the buying rate at N1,450 per dollar and the selling rate at N1,470. The local currency had traded at N1,430 per dollar on Monday, compared with N1,390 on November 13, representing a depreciation of N40, or 2.88 per cent. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the official window, the naira also weakened to N1,363.23 per dollar. Data from the NFEM showed that the currency depreciated by N7.43, or 0.55 per cent, from the N1,355.80 per dollar recorded on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s foreign exchange reserves stood at $43.64 billion as of November 14, compared with $45.56 billion recorded on January 2. The figures, obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), indicated a decline of $1.92 billion, or 4.21 per cent, in the country’s external reserves since the beginning of the year. In a related development, the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) on Wednesday signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, energy financing and macroeconomic stability. items.title: NNPC, CBN sign deal to boost oil production to 3m bpd
items.description: By Udeme Akpan The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, improve financial discipline and attract investment into the country’s energy sector. The agreement, signed at the CBN headquarters in Abuja on Wednesday, is also expected to support NNPC’s ambition to increase Nigeria’s crude oil production from the current 1.8 million barrels per day to three million barrels per day. Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr. Bashir Bayo Ojulari, described the agreement as a defining moment in the relationship between the national oil company and the country’s monetary authority. He said the MoU established a structured framework for collaboration between both institutions at the intersection of energy and finance. “This MoU provides that structure by which the two institutions will collaborate at the meeting point between energy and finance,” Ojulari said. He explained that the partnership would support NNPC’s initiatives, strengthen the flow of export proceeds into the Nigerian economy, address foreign exchange challenges affecting trade and improve financing arrangements for energy projects. According to him, the agreement would also help the company raise capital based on its balance sheet and assets, with guidance from the CBN. “We are here to build a working partnership that delivers results,” he said. Providing further details, NNPC’s Group Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Adedapo Segun, said the agreement would replace previous practices of addressing financial issues through irregular arrangements with a more coordinated and structured approach. He explained that improved coordination between the two institutions would help attract the investment required to raise crude oil production from 1.8 million barrels per day to three million barrels per day. On implementation, Segun said NNPC would align domestic payments, contractor settlements and foreign exchange conversions with CBN regulations to support the stability of the naira and reduce dollarisation. He added that both institutions had agreed to establish working groups, implementation timelines and accountability mechanisms to ensure effective execution of the MoU. The Treasurer of NNPC Limited, Mr. John Etukudo, will oversee implementation on behalf of the company. On his part, the CBN Governor, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, described the agreement as a formalisation of an existing relationship between the two institutions. He said their collaboration in account management, fund transfers and liquidity support would contribute to macroeconomic stability by ensuring the availability of revenue for government fiscal obligations and predictable foreign exchange inflows. “Our continued collaboration in efficient account management, funds transfer and liquidity support directly contributes to macroeconomic stability by ensuring the availability of revenue to achieve fiscal mandates and predictable inflows into the foreign exchange markets,” Cardoso said. items.title: Moov Africa Burkina : Les débits du Wi-Fi Fibre doublés et les tarifs revus à la baisse dès le 27 novembre 2026
items.description: Moov Africa Burkina annonce le doublement des débits de ses offres Wi-Fi Fibre et une baisse des tarifs de ses abonnements. L'annonce a été faite au cours d'une conférence de presse tenue ce mercredi 18 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Ces nouvelles mesures entreront en vigueur le 27 novembre prochain. Les abonnés de Moov Africa Burkina pourront bientôt profiter d'une connexion internet plus rapide sans augmentation de leur facture. Au cours d'une conférence de presse organisée le mercredi 18 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, l'opérateur a dévoilé ses nouvelles dispositions commerciales, qui concernent aussi bien les anciens que les nouveaux clients. À partir du 27 novembre 2026, tous les abonnés au Wi-Fi Fibre verront leur débit de connexion doubler automatiquement, sans augmentation de leur facture mensuelle. Ainsi, un abonnement de 50 Mbps passera à 100 Mbps, tandis qu'une offre de 100 Mbps évoluera à 200 Mbps. Cette augmentation sera effectuée à distance, sans formalités administratives, sans déplacement en agence et sans changement d'équipement. Les clients pourront ainsi profiter de ces nouvelles performances tout en conservant leurs avantages habituels. Dès le 27 novembre 2026, Moov Africa Burkina entend proposer à sa clientèle des débits Wi-Fi Fibre doublés et des abonnements à tarifs réduits. En plus du doublement des débits, Moov Africa Burkina annonce une baisse des tarifs de ses abonnements à la fibre optique. À titre d'illustration, une nouvelle souscription à une offre de 100 Mbps, qui coûtait auparavant 24 900 FCFA, sera désormais proposée à 15 000 FCFA à compter du 27 novembre 2026. Pour les nouveaux souscripteurs, l'opérateur annonce également des réductions significatives sur ses offres de fibre optique. Celles-ci pourront atteindre 65 %, selon les formules proposées. Cette mesure vise à lever les obstacles financiers à l'accès au très haut débit et à permettre à un plus grand nombre de Burkinabè de bénéficier d'une connexion à des tarifs plus accessibles. Les personnes intéressées pourront également demander l'installation de la fibre optique à leur domicile après avoir vérifié leur éligibilité, directement depuis l'application Moov Money, sans avoir à se déplacer en agence. L'opérateur affiche par ailleurs ses ambitions dans le domaine de l'ultra-haut débit. Dès le 27 novembre 2026, il prévoit de commercialiser une offre pouvant atteindre 500 Mbps. Selon Moov Africa ONATEL, cette formule fera de l'entreprise le seul fournisseur d'accès à internet au Burkina Faso à proposer un tel niveau de débit. Quelques-unes des offres et des avantages de la fibre optique de Moov Africa Burkina. Selon Idogo Mamadou, chef du département marketing, communication produit et digital de Moov Africa Burkina, cette initiative répond à l'évolution des habitudes de consommation et aux besoins croissants en bande passante. « Aujourd'hui, les usages évoluent. Les applications sont de plus en plus gourmandes en besoin de bande passante. D'où l'idée pour nous de faire ces augmentations du débit pour assurer une meilleure expérience à nos fidèles clients », a-t-il expliqué. À travers ces nouvelles dispositions, Moov Africa Burkina entend contribuer à l'amélioration de l'expérience numérique de ses abonnés, qu'il s'agisse de particuliers ou d'entreprises. L'opérateur ambitionne notamment de poursuivre le développement d'offres adaptées aux besoins des différentes catégories de clients. Idogo Mamadou, chef du département marketing, communication produit et digital de Moov Africa Burkina. « Les perspectives pour nous, c'est vraiment de continuer à accélérer la transformation digitale, non seulement de nos clients résidentiels, mais aussi des entreprises », a indiqué Mamadou Idogo. Le responsable marketing a également souligné la volonté de l'opérateur d'enrichir ses offres avec des services à valeur ajoutée. L'objectif, selon lui, est de faire de la connexion internet davantage qu'un simple accès au réseau, en proposant aux abonnés une expérience numérique plus complète. Jean Élysée Nikiéma Dalilha Ky Lefaso.net

items.title: Mine murder: Court fixes December 21 for judgment
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — A Delta State High Court sitting in Asaba has fixed December 21, 2026, for judgment in the trial of Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Usman Nuhu, popularly known as Ogbegbe, and four others over the fatal shooting of Oghenemine Ogidi, alias Mine, in Effurun, Delta State. The date was fixed on Tuesday after the prosecution and defence adopted their respective final written addresses, bringing proceedings in the case to a close ahead of judgment. Justice Michael Obi, who presided over the trial, adjourned the matter after listening to the final submissions of counsel to both parties. The five defendants are facing trial over the April 26 killing of Ogidi, an incident that attracted public attention and led to the dismissal of the police officers involved from the Nigeria Police Force. The prosecution had earlier closed its case after presenting six witnesses, following which the defendants opened and concluded their defence. Nuhu, the first defendant and principal suspect in the alleged shooting, remains in prison custody, while the court had earlier granted bail to the second to fifth defendants. The other defendants are Onoloko Dauroupamo, Okoh Kelechi, Goodluck Kingsley and Omonigho Ahweyevu. They were members of the anti-crime squad allegedly led by Nuhu at the Effurun Area Command before their dismissal following the incident. At an earlier sitting, counsel to Nuhu, Uche Chibuogwu, explained that the defence had deliberately refrained from filing a bail application for his client, citing concerns for his safety and the gravity of the murder charge. He said: “We did not find it necessary filing bail application for the first defendant, one, for his own safety, and secondly, this is a capital offence — offence of murder.” The Delta State Director of Public Prosecutions, Tejiri R. Anuwhin, had also explained that the four other defendants were granted bail because the offences they faced, bordering on negligence, carried a maximum six-month jail term. According to Anuwhin, the defendants had been in custody since June 1, making their continued detention potentially disproportionate to the maximum punishment prescribed for the alleged offences. With the adoption of final addresses by both parties, the court is expected to deliver its verdict on December 21, determining the culpability or otherwise of the defendants. items.title: Rent Commissioner disputes UGEL’s claim of student consultation over 15% rent increase
items.description: The Acting Rent Control Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, has disputed claims by the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL) that its 15 per cent rent increment was reached through consultation and agreement with students. According to him, student groups opposed the proposed increases during engagements with the university’s accommodation management and subsequently petitioned the Rent Control Department over the matter. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Wednesday, November 18, Mr Opoku criticised the University of Ghana’s Public Relations Officer over comments defending UGEL’s position, accusing the spokesperson of misrepresenting the concerns raised by students. “I’m very much disappointed in the PRO of the university. And it is that he said something that I want to dispute it and put it on point that it’s a palpable falsehood, not true. It is an imposition. That tells me today they are in bed with the UGEL people,” he said. Mr Opoku said he had engaged students over the past 11 months and received petitions from the University of Ghana Students’ Representative Council (SRC) and the Graduate Students’ Association of Ghana (GRASAG). According to him, the student groups had objected to successive proposals for rent increases, including 26 per cent, 19 per cent and 15 per cent, and questioned the basis for the adjustments. He therefore rejected the university’s position that the final 15 per cent increase followed consultations and an agreement with students. “It’s not true. Leave them. Consultation with who? I’m saying that I have a letter that today, if you put them on the spot, the GRASAG and the SRC, if they were elected by their students and they will be loyal to their students, not to be in bed with management, they should be honest and tell us,” he said. The Acting Rent Control Commissioner argued that UGEL’s status as a private commercial entity does not exempt it from rent regulation. He said the company’s business of providing accommodation in exchange for payment falls within the scope of activities regulated by the Rent Control Department. “The lady claims that UGEL is a private entity. So who regulates the private people?” he asked. Mr Opoku maintained that operating within the University of Ghana does not place UGEL beyond the reach of the law, adding that its commercial accommodation activities must comply with applicable rent regulations. “You are doing commercial business, and you have a board. So if there’s a regulator that ensures that space that you take money, you give property, it’s rent. The actions and their activity automatically bring them there. And the fact that they operate in Legon does not insulate them. And that’s what they should begin to understand,” he added.

items.title: Nescafé Real Vibes Promo rewards Kumasi winners with exciting goodies in third draw
items.description: The Nescafé Real Vibes promo continues to offer exciting giveaways to customers as Kumasi hosted the third draw of the nationwide promotion. The event held at Kejetia in Kumasi attracted a large crowd of traders, shoppers, and Nescafé lovers who gathered to witness the selection of winners live. The ongoing national promo is rewarding consumers across the country with exciting packages, including an ultimate prize of a car and several other goodies. In the third draw, one customer won the seed capital of GHS 10,000, while two others won the top cash prizes of GHS 5,000 MoMo each. Six laptops were given to other winners to assist their digital skills at work and school, while four winners took home smartphones to stay connected. Nine winners grabbed power banks for “power on the go”, and one hundred (100) winners received 100-cedi mobile money cash each, with ten others winning GHS 50 mobile money cash each. Ralph Rockson took home the ultimate prize, a car, after making 111 attempts to clinch the top prize. His win was cited by the organisers as proof that persistence and consistent participation could pay off, since the draw is based solely on chances. Category Development Manager for Nescafé at Nestlé Ghana, Lily Boatemaa Ntim, said Kumasi was chosen for the third draw because it is one of the biggest markets for Nescafé in Ghana. “We chose to come here this time because Kumasi is one of our biggest cities when it comes to Nescafé, and so we decided to come and draw one of the ultimate prizes, which is the car, here,” she said. She explained that the draw was held publicly to educate consumers on how to enter into the promo and also to prove that the process is not rigged, but is transparent and fair to all participants. Ms Boatemaa added that the presence of the National Lottery Authority, together with members of the public who were invited to take part in the draw, was to build confidence and show that every entry stands an equal chance of winning, regardless of the region or the number of attempts. “We had NLA here so that they know how the draw is run. We have not rigged anything. We have people who are actually genuinely entering into it. Some people entered five, and they won. Others did 111, and they won. Others did 406, and they won. So, it’s a game of chance, and NLA is supervising this to ensure that it is fair and it is also just,” she stressed. She disclosed that two more draws remain, including the grand draw, with one more car, cash, laptops, motorbikes, iPhones and Samsung phones still to be won. According to her, the remaining draws would offer another opportunity for those who did not win in Kumasi to try their luck. She urged residents of the Ashanti Region to increase their entries to stand a chance of winning, noting that although a lot of entries are coming from the region, the number is still not enough compared to the prizes available. “You need five sachets to be able to enter into the draw, and you dial *380*9#. You could be the ultimate winner of the other car. The other car is red, and December is a red Christmas. So maybe it could be your chance. So don’t listen and hear people win. Be the winner,” she said. The Category Development Manager for Nescafé revealed that the promo packs, with ‘Win up to one million’ on them, are available in every shop, and buying a whole strip gives consumers two entries. She explained that consumers only need to buy the pack, empty it, find the unique code inside each sachet, and submit their codes by dialing *380*9# on their phone to participate. Eric Inusah, a customer from Kumasi who won a laptop in the Nescafé Real Vibes Promo Draw, said he initially doubted the authenticity of the promotion. Speaking after receiving his prize, Inusah admitted he had been sceptical when he first entered, but receiving the laptop had changed his perception completely. “At first, I thought it was not real. But now that I have received my laptop, I will tell all my friends and family that it is not fake and they should also take part,” he said. Inusah added that the laptop would help him greatly in his work and studies, and expressed his gratitude to Nescafé for delivering on its promise.

items.title: Niger miners’ deaths: Senate demands sanctions, compensation
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has urged the Federal Government to expedite the implementation of recommendations made by the independent investigative committee into the deaths of 37 artisanal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State. The lawmakers specifically called for accountability, appropriate sanctions against officers found culpable and institutional reforms within the NSCDC, warning that further delay in implementing the recommendations could undermine public confidence in the government’s commitment to justice. The Senate also stressed the need for prompt payment of financial compensation recommended for the families of the deceased. The resolutions followed a motion on Wednesday sponsored by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Finance, Senator Sani Musa (APC, Niger East), and co-sponsored by 18 other senators from the North-Central geopolitical zone and Senator Nasir Sani Zango Daura (APC, Katsina North). The Senate commended President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Government for establishing an independent investigative committee to probe the incident and acknowledged that the 10-member panel, chaired by Jonathan Kure, had submitted its report. The committee reportedly identified serious lapses and recommended sanctions, institutional reforms and financial compensation for the victims’ families and other affected persons. The lawmakers recalled that the 37 miners died on September 17, 2026, while in NSCDC custody in Minna, Niger State, after reportedly being arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining activities. They expressed concern that the circumstances surrounding the deaths raised serious questions about the protection of fundamental human rights and the responsibility of security agencies to safeguard persons in their custody. The Senate warned that any further delay in implementing the committee’s recommendations, particularly the payment of compensation, would prolong the suffering of the bereaved families. It also called for comprehensive reforms in the management of detention facilities and the operational procedures of security agencies to prevent a recurrence. Seconding the motion, Senator Ned Nwoko (APC, Delta North) described the incident as a national tragedy, insisting that the circumstances of the deaths should be examined objectively, irrespective of the alleged activities of the deceased. He said: “It is a national tragedy when so many young lives are lost under circumstances such as the ones we are discussing.” Nwoko, who drew parallels with incidents involving young people allegedly engaged in illegal activities in oil-producing communities in the South-South, said the country must apply consistent standards in addressing such cases. He added: “The fact that some of these young men may have been involved in illegal activities should not mean that their lives are not valued. “Life is life, regardless of the circumstances. We should be consistent in how we respond to such incidents.” The Senate also resolved to constitute a delegation, to be led by the President of the Senate or his nominee, to pay a condolence visit to Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, and the bereaved families. The delegation will comprise relevant senators, particularly those from Niger State and the North-Central zone, and will formally convey the Senate’s condolences and solidarity. It further directed its relevant committees, particularly those on Interior, Solid Minerals, Human Rights, Police Affairs and Judiciary, to exercise oversight on the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations and report progress to the chamber. In his presentation, Musa said the deaths had left families and communities devastated, underscoring the need for institutional accountability, respect for human dignity and strict adherence to established laws and procedures in the treatment of persons in custody. He said the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations was essential to demonstrating the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and fundamental rights of Nigerians. During deliberations, Senator Adams Oshiomhole (APC, Edo North) proposed an additional prayer condemning illegal mining and urging traditional rulers, state governments and local government authorities to sensitise their communities against the practice. Oshiomhole argued that while the Senate was concerned about the deaths, it should also make clear its opposition to illegal mining, which he described as an attempt to divert the country’s mineral resources into private pockets. The additional prayer was seconded by Senator Simon Lalong (APC, Plateau South). However, Senator Abdul Ningi (PDP, Bauchi Central), raising a point of order under Order 56 of the Senate Standing Orders, challenged the relevance of the additional prayer to the substantive motion. Ningi argued that the motion was specifically about the deaths of the 37 miners in NSCDC custody and the need to implement the investigative committee’s recommendations, not illegal mining. He maintained that the issue was fundamentally about humanity and the circumstances surrounding the deaths. Ruling on the point of order, Senate President Godswill Akpabio upheld Ningi’s objection, effectively dropping the additional prayer. Akpabio said the Senate’s concern was to ensure justice for the deceased and their families, stressing that the miners were entitled to the presumption of innocence under the law. He said: “The Nigerian law presumes every person innocent until proven guilty. That is the most important point here. “The reason the Senate is sympathetic towards the deceased is that they had not been found guilty of any offence. If they had been prosecuted, they would have had the opportunity to defend themselves.” The Senate President said the deceased had died under tragic and questionable circumstances without being given the opportunity to defend themselves before a competent court. He added that the ongoing investigation should not be prejudged but stressed that the circumstances of the deaths warranted the Senate’s intervention. Akpabio said the motion was necessary to bring the incident to national attention, adding that the Senate would continue to monitor efforts to ensure justice for the victims and their families. The chamber thereafter observed a minute of silence in honour of the 37 deceased miners. The post Niger miners’ deaths: Senate demands sanctions, compensation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Businessman and philanthropist Alhaji Fuzak calls for community support for schools
items.description: Ghanaian businessman and philanthropist Alhaji Fuseini Yushaw, popularly known as Alhaji Fuzak, has called on the government, institutions and individuals to invest in education by supporting the development of school infrastructure. He said providing quality learning facilities was essential to empowering the next generation, reducing illiteracy and preparing young people for leadership. “The best cement is for classrooms, not mansions. The school we are commissioning today will help curb illiteracy and produce future leaders,” he said. Addressing participants at the commissioning of a classroom block in Tamale, Alhaji Fuzak urged prominent individuals in Dagbon to contribute to the development of their communities rather than rely solely on government support. “We cannot wait for the government alone to provide everything for us. The government will do its part, but we, as sons of the North, must also develop our communities,” he said. He also stressed the importance of girls’ education, urging parents and communities to ensure that girls are given the opportunity to attend school and pursue their ambitions. “I want to see our daughters in school and not at home. When you educate a girl, you educate a whole community,” he said. Alhaji Fuzak encouraged students to take their education seriously, drawing on his personal journey to inspire them to aspire to greater achievements. “I was once like you, sitting at a wooden desk. Today, I build schools, and tomorrow, you could do the same. So take your education seriously and study hard,” he said. He further urged teachers to remain disciplined, committed and supportive of their pupils, emphasising their responsibility in shaping the lives of young people. “To the teachers: be disciplined and love the children. Your reward is in heaven, and Allah will give it to you,” he said. The philanthropist also appealed to the school’s management and the surrounding community to take responsibility for protecting and maintaining the newly commissioned facility. “To the community and chiefs: this building has been handed over, but the job is not done. Please protect it, and let us establish a school management committee to ensure it is well maintained for generations to come. May this school produce leaders who will bring peace to Dagbon and Ghana,” he said.
