items.title: Du laboratoire au champ : le long chemin des variétés de riz améliorées au Burkina Faso
items.description: SOURA Sibiri¹ ¹ Centre national de la recherche scientifique et technologique (CNRST), Burkina Faso Auteur correspondant : SOURA Sibiri, Email : sibiri.soura@cnrst.gov.bf Introduction Le riz occupe une place croissante dans l'alimentation des Burkinabè. Or, la production nationale couvre moins de la moitié des besoins, et le pays doit importer le reste. Pourtant, les solutions techniques existent. En effet, depuis les années 1970, la recherche agricole nationale, portée par l'Institut de l'environnement et de recherches agricoles (INERA), a mis au point plus de cinquante variétés de riz à haut rendement, adaptées aux périmètres irrigués, aux bas-fonds et à la culture sous pluie. Cependant, ces variétés ne donnent pas dans les champs ce qu'elles donnent dans les stations de recherche. Alors qu'elles peuvent produire 5 à 7 tonnes par hectare, la plupart des exploitations récoltent entre 1 et 2,6 tonnes par hectare en riziculture pluviale et de bas-fonds (Koutou et al., 2021 ; Yaméogo et al., 2019). L'écart est donc considérable. Dès lors, cet article explique pourquoi les variétés améliorées peinent à passer du laboratoire au champ. Il montre que ce passage n'est pas un simple transfert technique. Il dépend en effet du prix des semences et des engrais, de la présence des agents de conseil, du jugement des producteurs eux-mêmes et du travail de leurs organisations. Ces résultats s'adressent d'abord aux producteurs et à leurs organisations, mais aussi aux agents de vulgarisation, aux services agricoles, aux ONG et aux chercheurs. Ils aident ainsi à repérer où le chemin se bloque, et sur quels relais s'appuyer pour le débloquer. Méthodologie L'étude repose sur une démarche qualitative : elle cherche à comprendre les raisons d'agir des acteurs plutôt qu'à mesurer des quantités. Elle combine deux sources d'information. D'une part, l'auteur a examiné des documents : stratégies nationales de développement de la riziculture, rapports des administrations et des institutions de recherche, travaux scientifiques sur la filière. D'autre part, quinze entretiens ont été réalisés à Ouagadougou entre mai et août 2025. Les personnes interrogées étaient des chercheurs d'instituts nationaux, des cadres de l'administration et des responsables d'organisations paysannes ou semencières, notamment la Confédération paysanne du Faso et l'Union nationale des producteurs semenciers du Burkina. Les entretiens ont ensuite été transcrits, puis codés à l'aide du logiciel QualCoder selon une analyse thématique. Autrement dit, les propos ont été regroupés par thèmes, par exemple les obstacles à l'utilisation des résultats, les relations entre chercheurs et producteurs ou le rôle des intermédiaires. En outre, ces propos ont été confrontés aux documents et aux chiffres disponibles sur la filière, afin de vérifier les faits. Il convient toutefois de préciser que l'étude ne mesure pas elle-même les rendements : elle s'appuie sur les données existantes et analyse ce que les acteurs font des innovations. Cette démarche a permis de dégager quatre résultats, présentés ci-dessous dans un ordre logique : d'abord l'ampleur de l'écart entre la station et le champ, ensuite les obstacles concrets, puis la manière dont les producteurs s'approprient les variétés, enfin le rôle des organisations paysannes. Résultats 1. Un écart important entre la station de recherche et le champ Le premier résultat mesure la distance qui sépare la recherche des exploitations. En effet, les variétés améliorées atteignent 5 à 7 tonnes par hectare en station, alors que les rendements réels se situent entre 1 et 2,6 tonnes par hectare dans les systèmes pluviaux et les bas-fonds non aménagés. De même, les semences certifiées, c'est-à-dire contrôlées et garanties, ne sont utilisées qu'à hauteur d'environ 11,7 % au niveau national. Toutefois, cette moyenne cache une forte différence entre les zones. Dans les grands périmètres irrigués, où les variétés améliorées sont imposées par les cahiers des charges, leur utilisation approche les 100 %. En revanche, elle reste marginale dans le reste du pays. Par conséquent, l'objectif fixé par la stratégie nationale de développement de la riziculture, qui vise 85 % de semences certifiées et 3 millions de tonnes de riz paddy à l'horizon 2030, suppose de lever des obstacles bien précis. 2. Des obstacles concrets : le prix, le conseil et l'information Le deuxième résultat identifie ces obstacles. Le premier est le coût. En effet, les semences améliorées se vendent entre 800 et 1 000 francs CFA le kilo, alors que les producteurs manquent souvent d'argent disponible au moment des semis (Ouattara et al., 2021). De plus, les engrais sont chers, la mécanisation est faible et le crédit agricole reste difficile d'accès. À cela s'ajoutent les retards de livraison des intrants subventionnés, qui arrivent parfois trop tard pour la campagne. Le deuxième obstacle est le manque de conseil de proximité. Ainsi, un agent d'appui-conseil couvre couramment sept à huit villages, alors que la norme recommandée est de cinq. Par ailleurs, beaucoup de producteurs ne savent pas lire, ce qui limite leur accès à l'information technique. Le troisième obstacle tient à la circulation de l'information elle-même. Pendant longtemps, en effet, la recherche a fonctionné du haut vers le bas : le chercheur trouvait, l'agent technique diffusait, le paysan appliquait. « Les chercheurs n'attendaient aucun feed-back des paysans », se souvient un chercheur à la retraite. Or, ce défaut de dialogue n'a pas entièrement disparu. Un cadre du ministère en charge de l'agriculture le constate : « Les travaux des chercheurs généralement ne sont même pas connus à l'interne par leurs collègues, encore moins à l'extérieur par les utilisateurs potentiels ». 3. Des producteurs qui jugent, adaptent et contournent Le troisième résultat montre que les producteurs ne reçoivent pas les innovations passivement. Au contraire, ils les évaluent selon leurs propres critères. À la Vallée du Kou, par exemple, ils ont donné aux variétés de l'INERA des noms tirés de leur quotidien (Ouoba et al., 2023) : « Macaroni » pour la FKR62N, en raison de la longueur de son grain et de son goût ; « Fantan dèmè », c'est-à-dire « l'aide aux pauvres », pour la FKR28, parce qu'elle demande peu d'engrais ; « 4×4 » pour la FKR19, parce qu'elle s'adapte à tous les terrains. Ces noms révèlent ce qui compte pour les producteurs : le goût, l'économie d'intrants et la robustesse, et pas seulement le rendement maximal. D'ailleurs, beaucoup de techniques ont été adoptées sans bruit. « Beaucoup de technologies ont été intégrées par les producteurs dans leurs activités […]. Malheureusement tous les résultats ne sont pas perceptibles tellement les gens les ont intégrés », observe un responsable d'organisation paysanne. Cependant, l'adoption a aussi un coût social. En effet, dans les périmètres aménagés, le calendrier de culture est strict : dates de pépinière, repiquage en ligne, désherbage, traitements. Il laisse donc moins de temps à la vie familiale et communautaire. De plus, pour acheter semences, engrais et services mécanisés, les producteurs doivent emprunter. Il en résulte que l'argent prend une place nouvelle dans les familles : l'autorité des chefs de famille s'affaiblit, tandis que des cadets ou des femmes étuveuses gagnent en autonomie grâce au commerce du riz. C'est pourquoi de nombreux producteurs gardent des solutions de rechange. Ils continuent ainsi à échanger des semences par le troc ou le don, et à sélectionner eux-mêmes leurs meilleurs grains. Ce faisant, ils préservent leur liberté de choix et la diversité de leurs variétés. 4. Les organisations paysannes, traductrices entre chercheurs et producteurs Le quatrième résultat met en avant un acteur décisif. En effet, entre le laboratoire et le champ, il faut des intermédiaires capables de parler aux deux mondes. Ce rôle revient de plus en plus aux organisations paysannes, comme la Confédération paysanne du Faso (CPF), l'Union nationale des producteurs de riz du Burkina (UNPRB) et l'Union nationale des producteurs semenciers (UNPSB). Ces organisations accomplissent un double travail. D'une part, elles expliquent aux riziculteurs, dans un langage accessible, les résultats de la recherche et les exigences techniques des nouvelles variétés. D'autre part, elles font remonter aux décideurs et aux partenaires financiers les contraintes réelles du monde rural et le savoir pratique des producteurs. En outre, elles permettent de négocier collectivement avec les rizeries et les banques, notamment dans la plaine de Bama et à Bagré. Les chercheurs eux-mêmes passent par elles : « Je travaille également avec le monde agricole, surtout les organisations avec qui j'implémente les résultats de mes recherches », explique un agronome. Grâce à ce travail, d'autres façons de produire ont été reconnues par les politiques publiques, à côté de la grande irrigation : l'aménagement des bas-fonds ou le système de riziculture intensive, par exemple. Néanmoins, ce relais reste fragile. En effet, une variété peut être abandonnée si les producteurs la jugent trop coûteuse ou peu conforme au goût local. Autrement dit, une innovation ne dure que si ceux qui la cultivent continuent d'y trouver leur intérêt. Conclusion En définitive, l'étude montre que le faible usage des variétés améliorées de riz ne s'explique pas par un refus du progrès. Il s'explique plutôt par des obstacles précis et par des choix raisonnés des producteurs. Trois enseignements se dégagent. D'abord, l'écart entre la station et le champ tient surtout au prix des semences et des engrais, au manque de conseil et à une information qui circule difficilement. Ensuite, les producteurs jugent les variétés selon leurs propres critères, les adaptent et gardent leurs réseaux d'échange de semences. Enfin, les organisations paysannes sont devenues le relais indispensable entre chercheurs, producteurs et décideurs. Ainsi, pour les chercheurs et les services agricoles, la leçon est d'associer les producteurs dès le choix des variétés et de tenir compte du goût, du coût et de la robustesse. Quant aux organisations paysannes, l'étude confirme l'utilité de leur rôle de traduction et de négociation. Autrement dit, une variété ne devient une réussite que lorsqu'elle est à la fois performante, accessible et acceptée. Ce document de vulgarisation est tiré de l'article scientifique : SOURA, Sibiri (2026), « Gouverner l'agriculture par la preuve ? Usages et mises en scène de l'expertise rizicole au Burkina Faso », Afrilex , p. 1‑27. Contraintes de développement et opportunités d'investissement privé , Rome, FAO. OUATTARA, Issa, TRAORE, Arahama et KABORE, Amado (2021), « Analyse des contraintes à la vulgarisation des résultats de la recherche agricole de l'Institut de l'Environnement et de Recherches Agricoles (INERA) du Burkina Faso », Science et technique, Sciences Naturelles et Appliquées , vol. 40, n° 2, p. 86-98. items.title: Madina MP Francis-Xavier Sosu returns to Parliament after collapsing at GIMPA
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Madina, Francis-Xavier Sosu, has returned to Parliament after collapsing while delivering a speech at the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA), marking his first appearance in the House since the incident. Dr Sosu received a warm welcome from fellow Members of Parliament as he resumed parliamentary duties, using the opportunity to reflect on the health scare, his recovery and the support he received during the difficult period. In his first parliamentary remarks since the incident, the legislator expressed gratitude to those who stood by him, acknowledging the support of his political party, Parliament, his constituents in Madina and the medical professionals who attended to him. Speaking to Adom News in Parliament, Dr Sosu recounted the experience and said the period of recovery had offered him important lessons about the need to prioritise personal health, particularly for people holding public office. He advised public officers not to take their health for granted, stressing that the incident was a reminder that nobody is immune to health challenges, regardless of their position or responsibilities. He also expressed appreciation to the doctors and nurses at the University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC) for the care and attention they provided during his recovery. The MP extended his gratitude to his party and Parliament for standing by him, as well as the people of Madina whose concern and support, he said, helped him through the difficult period. How the GIMPA incident happened Dr Sosu collapsed on Thursday, September 24, 2026, while delivering a speech at GIMPA in Accra. He was addressing students on his personal experiences, leadership and commitment to public service when he appeared to lose consciousness on stage. Moments before collapsing, he had urged his audience to embrace servant leadership, saying: “I respectfully submit that if you want to be a good leader, let service be your hallmark.” People at the event immediately rushed to his assistance. Although he briefly appeared to regain consciousness and seemed ready to continue his address, he subsequently slumped again and was helped off the stage for medical attention. CitiNewsroom.com+1

items.title: BoG to assess rural banks’ conversion progress before considering extensions
items.description: The Bank of Ghana says it is open to considering extensions for rural banks that are unable to meet the December 2026 deadline for transitioning into community banks, as it continues to engage institutions on the conversion process. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, said the central bank was in discussions with rural banks to ensure a smooth transition, adding that institutions facing difficulties would be considered on a case-by-case basis. Speaking at the 133rd Monetary Policy Committee press briefing, Dr Asiama said the December deadline remained in place, but the Bank was flexible enough to accommodate institutions that may require additional time. “We gave the end-of-December deadline. But even then, we are in conversation with the rural banks. Those that make it, yes. Those that are not able to make it, will require some consideration. Of course, we are flexible enough to work with them,” he said. The Governor urged rural banks to take advantage of the transition to community banks, which is expected to strengthen their operations and improve their capacity to serve customers. “We want to urge them, as many of them as possible, to take that transition to community banks,” Dr Asiama said. He also indicated that the Bank was engaging commercial banks on the implementation of the minimum capital requirements directive, with a meeting scheduled with bank chief executives next week to discuss the matter. According to the Governor, the central bank would continue working with affected institutions and consider extensions where necessary, depending on their circumstances and progress made. “If there’s a need to extend or to consider for any of them, that will be based on the fact. And so far, we see the progress that has been made is quite satisfactory, and we’ll continue to work on it,” he added. The developments come as the Bank of Ghana continues efforts to strengthen the banking sector, improve the resilience of financial institutions and expand access to financial services across the country.

El documento completo se publicará en los próximos días, pero fuentes conocedoras de ese documento han ofrecido detalles sobre el calendario y los hitos que se prevén: en 2040 el 100% de la electricidad se cubrirá con energías renovables y el uso de combustibles fósiles habrá desaparecido por completo en el sector residencial, el primario y la movilidad urbana. items.title: Tinubu approves world’s first PR university, says Nigeria bigger than 419
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of what he described as the world’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, as part of efforts to develop a new generation of communication professionals through specialised education, research and professional training. Tinubu announced the approval in a speech delivered by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. The President said a major outcome of Nigeria’s hosting of the global forum was the determination to establish a lasting institutional legacy for the public relations profession. He said: “In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines.” He described the proposed institution as a major investment in human capital and the future of communication, adding that it would provide opportunities to develop communication leaders capable of responding to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment. Tinubu commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, and the Nasarawa State Government for their collaboration and commitment to the initiative. He urged stakeholders to work together to ensure that the institution developed into a centre of excellence. The President also expressed Nigeria’s appreciation to the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the international public relations community for entrusting the country with the hosting of the global gathering. He described the decision as recognition of Nigeria’s growing contribution to the global communication profession and its capacity to promote responsible communication. Tinubu said hosting the forum provided an opportunity to showcase Nigeria’s people, cultural diversity, economic potential and commitment to constructive international engagement. Addressing the changing communication landscape, the President said digital technologies and artificial intelligence were transforming how information was created, distributed and consumed. He, however, warned that the developments had also created challenges, including misinformation, disinformation, hate speech and declining public trust. “In this environment, public relations and communication professionals have responsibilities that go beyond managing images and reputations,” he said. According to him, communication professionals must promote truth, accountability, transparency, mutual understanding and constructive engagement between governments, institutions and citizens. Tinubu also urged international delegates to look beyond the conference and explore Nigeria’s economic and investment opportunities. Highlighting the country’s technology ecosystem, he said six of Africa’s 10 unicorn companies were Nigerian, listing Flutterwave, OPay, Interswitch, Moove and Moniepoint among the companies. The President also praised the resilience, confidence and hard work of Nigerians, describing himself as a “swashbuckling capitalist”. He said Nigerians were generally confident and hardworking, adding that the country’s population and global influence would continue to grow. According to him, one out of every four black men is Nigerian, a proportion he projected would rise to one in three by 2050. He further projected that Nigeria would surpass the United States to become the world’s third most populous country, with an estimated population of 440 million by 2050. Defending Nigeria’s international image, Tinubu said the country should not be defined by negative social media stereotypes and internet fraud, commonly referred to as 419. He cited the educational achievements of Nigerians in the United States, claiming that 60 per cent of Nigerian Americans held college degrees. “So Nigeria goes beyond 419. Nigeria is much more bigger than that,” he said. The post Tinubu approves world’s first PR university, says Nigeria bigger than 419 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Chimamanda’s son’s death: Coroner resumes inquest
items.description: The coroner’s inquest into the death of Nkanu Adichie-Esege, son of Nigerian author Chimamanda Adichie and her husband, Ivara Esege, resumed on Wednesday at the Igbosere Magistrate’s Court in Lagos following a Lagos High Court ruling affirming the coroner’s jurisdiction. The coroner, Magistrate Atinuke Adetunji, resumed proceedings after the High Court dismissed an application by Euracare Hospital seeking to stop the inquest. At Wednesday’s sitting, Taiwo Osipitan, counsel to Euracare Hospital, said it was the first time all parties were appearing before the coroner following the conclusion of proceedings at the High Court. Osipitan said the High Court had ruled that the matter had not reached the stage at which judicial review was necessary and directed that the case be returned to the coroner’s court for continuation of the inquest. He subsequently tendered a copy of the High Court judgment before Adetunji. However, Chukwudi Enebeli, counsel to the deceased’s family, told the court that Euracare’s application was struck out because the coroner’s court had jurisdiction to proceed with the inquest. Enebeli sought an adjournment, explaining that Euracare had only served the parties in open court with the witness statement on oath of Tosin Majekodunmi, a medical doctor. He said the family needed time to examine the statement and determine whether a response would be necessary. Abiodun Loyonu, counsel to Atlantis Paediatric Hospital, also asked the court for an opportunity to respond to Euracare’s witness statement. In her response, the magistrate reminded the parties that the inquest was inquisitorial in nature, adding that guidelines for conducting the proceedings had been discussed at a preliminary meeting held at the commencement of the inquiry. She urged all parties to bear the distinctive nature of the proceedings in mind as the inquest progressed. The coroner also asked whether the parties had filed witness statements on oath in preparation for the hearing. Osipitan, however, sought clarification on whether Lagos State Government officials would be required to file witness statements on oath or could appear in court to give oral evidence if subpoenaed. Adetunji said filing witness statements on oath was not mandatory for such witnesses, adding that government officials summoned through subpoenas could appear before the court and give oral evidence. The parties subsequently agreed that the deceased’s family would lead evidence, followed by Atlantis Paediatric Hospital and Euracare Hospital. The coroner adjourned the inquest to January 19, 20 and 28, 2027. Nkanu, one of Adichie’s twins, died on January 7, 2026, following complications during a series of preparatory medical procedures at Euracare Hospital after being referred from Atlantis Paediatric Hospital. The coroner commenced the inquest in February to establish the circumstances surrounding the 21-month-old child’s death. Proceedings earlier revealed that the child’s body had been cremated, raising questions about the availability of primary forensic evidence. Euracare subsequently approached the Lagos High Court, seeking a judicial review of the coroner’s jurisdiction, particularly in view of the cremation. In June, the High Court ordered a temporary suspension of the inquest pending a judicial review of how the proceedings were initiated and conducted. The coroner subsequently adjourned the matter to October. However, in October, the High Court, presided over by Justice Aishat Opesanwo, rejected Euracare’s application to stop the inquest. The judge held that the coroner was legally constituted and that the cremation of the child’s body did not invalidate the decision to proceed with the inquiry. The post Chimamanda’s son’s death: Coroner resumes inquest appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NDC Ashanti regional constituency chairmen meet NAIMOS; pledge support for fight against galamsey
items.description: A delegation of NDC constituency chairmen from the Ashanti Region has pledged its support and collaboration with the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) in the ongoing fight against illegal mining. The pledge followed a meeting today, November 18, 2026, at the NAIMOS headquarters in Accra, where the delegation held discussions with the NAIMOS Director of Operations, Col. K. S. Appiah, and other officials of the Secretariat. The two parties discussed ways of strengthening grassroots cooperation, improving community relations and preventing violent confrontations, particularly in the wake of the November 11 Manso Keniago incident. Addressing the delegation, Col. Appiah expressed regret over the loss of lives and injuries recorded during the Manso Keniago incident, extended condolences to the affected families and reiterated NAIMOS’ support for transparent investigations into the circumstances surrounding the confrontation. He strongly urged the chairmen to caution their constituents against confronting armed military personnel undertaking lawful operations, stressing that such actions could result in avoidable casualties. He explained that persons whose excavators or other equipment are seized have appropriate legal and administrative channels through which they can seek redress without resorting to violence or aggressively confronting the NAIMOS task force. He clarified that NAIMOS is not opposed to lawful small-scale mining but stressed that mining in water bodies, protected forest reserves and other prohibited areas remains strictly forbidden. Col. Appiah further emphasised that NAIMOS would not sacrifice its enforcement mandate on the altar of political convenience, maintaining that the fight against illegal mining would be pursued firmly and impartially. The Director also addressed concerns about extortion and impersonation. In this regard, he stressed that NAIMOS has zero tolerance for bribery, extortion or any form of misconduct and encouraged community leaders to report suspicious individuals posing as security operatives. For their part, the constituency chairmen commended NAIMOS for its sustained efforts in combating illegal mining and pledged to deepen collaboration with the Secretariat through public education, dialogue and community sensitisation. They assured NAIMOS that they would convey the Director’s concerns to their respective constituents, intensify public education and discourage the growing tendency among some residents to confront or attack security personnel undertaking lawful anti-illegal mining operations. The chairmen further pledged to support efforts aimed at making illegal mining in water bodies, protected forest reserves and other prohibited areas a thing of the past. They also expressed their commitment to supporting the government’s Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme (rCOMSDEP) and rallying behind the sector minister, Hon. Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, in efforts to deal decisively with the menace of illegal mining. The meeting formed part of NAIMOS’ broader commitment to complement enforcement with sustained community engagement, dialogue and stakeholder collaboration in the fight against illegal mining.

items.description: ‎–Calls for vigilance against child sexual abuse ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has called on parents, educators, the media, and law enforcement agencies to remain vigilant and committed to protecting children from sexual exploitation, abuse, and violence. ‎ In a message marking the World Day for the Prevention of and Healing from Child Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Violence, Senator Tinubu urged Nigerians to reaffirm their collective duty to safeguard every child’s well-being. ‎ ‎“I call upon parents, educators, the media, and law enforcement agencies to remain vigilant and committed. We must protect our children at all times,” she said. ‎ ‎The First Lady stressed that no child should live in fear and that survivors must be treated with dignity. ‎ ‎“Every child deserves a childhood free from fear, and every survivor deserves our respect, compassion and support,” she stated. ‎ ‎Senator Oluremi Tinubu offered a prayer for the protection of children across the country: “May God protect all our children.” ‎ ‎The observance, marked annually on November 18, was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2022 to promote prevention, protection, and healing for children affected by sexual exploitation, abuse, and violence. ‎ ‎ The post ‎Every child deserves childhood free from fear — First Lady Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ADC campaign accuses INEC of bias, demands postponement of mock election test
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, of giving political parties inadequate notice for its November 28 mock accreditation and results collation exercise, demanding its postponement. The Council said the short notice would make it difficult for parties to mobilise, train and deploy agents for the nationwide exercise, warning that the process could undermine confidence in a test designed to assess electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC also faulted INEC’s reported decision not to upload results from Ward, Local Government and State collation levels to its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, during the 2027 elections. The Council said INEC’s November 16 notification, coming barely two days before the November 18 deadline for submitting agents’ names, was unfair, particularly as the exercise would cover all 774 Local Government Areas and two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 Registration Areas. “How does INEC expect political parties to adequately prepare, mobilise, train and submit their agents for an exercise of this magnitude within such a short time? This is not preparation; it is an ambush,” the Council queried. “INEC cannot test electoral credibility through an incredible process.” It demanded an immediate postponement to give political parties sufficient time to nominate agents and participate meaningfully. On electronic transmission of results, the ADC-PCC rejected comments reportedly made by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, that the Commission had neither developed nor tested the system for uploading results from the various collation levels. “Nigerians fought for and demanded real-time electronic transmission of election results precisely to eliminate the manipulation that often occurs between the Polling Unit and subsequent collation levels. “Any attempt to weaken, delay or abandon electronic transmission and public visibility of results at the various levels of collation is an invitation to electoral manipulation,” the Council warned. It recalled that former INEC Chairman, Professor Mahmood Yakubu, had promised to extend result uploads to Ward, Local Government and State levels, adding that his successor, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, had also pledged to strengthen electoral transparency. Questioning the Commission’s apparent change of position, the ADC-PCC asked: “What has changed? Why the sudden retreat from commitments previously made to Nigerians?” It further questioned why Forms EC8B (Ward), EC8C (Local Government) and EC8D (State) could not be uploaded to IReV when the Commission already had the technology to upload polling-unit results on Form EC8A. Warning against actions that could confer undue advantage on the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, the Council reminded INEC of its obligation to remain impartial. “INEC is not an extension of the ruling party. It is an independent electoral umpire, and it must act like one,” it declared. It warned Amupitan that his handling of the 2027 elections would shape his legacy and have consequences for the country’s peace. “His name, his legacy and the peace of this country are at stake. History will judge him not by assurances, but by the credibility of the elections he conducts,” the Council said. The ADC-PCC reaffirmed its commitment to defending electoral transparency and the sanctity of the ballot, declaring: “We will not be intimidated. We will not be silenced. We will continue to insist that every Nigerian’s vote must count.” The post ADC campaign accuses INEC of bias, demands postponement of mock election test appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lagos targets $1tr GDP by 2052, Sanwo-Olu declares
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has unveiled an ambitious target of growing the state’s economy to a $1 trillion Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2052, declaring that his administration is laying the foundation for Lagos to become one of the world’s leading sub-national economies. Sanwo-Olu, who disclosed this at the fourth Lagos State Employment Trust Fund (LSETF) Summit in Lagos on Wednesday, said the state’s budget had increased from less than ₦700 billion when he assumed office in 2019 to ₦4.2 trillion. He said the increased financial capacity was being deployed to promote shared prosperity, economic empowerment, infrastructure development and job creation. The summit, themed, “Lagos Works: Building Africa’s Most Productive City,” provided an opportunity for the governor to outline his administration’s economic development strategy and highlight the importance of institutional continuity in achieving sustainable growth. Sanwo-Olu described a productive city as one where workers generate higher economic value, businesses expand their customer base and households enjoy improved disposable incomes. According to him, achieving these objectives requires sustained investment in economic infrastructure, institutional capacity, private sector partnerships and employment-generating initiatives. He said: “Guided by our T.H.E.M.E.S. Plus agenda, we have systematically scaled our financial capacity to accelerate this prosperity. From an operating budget below ₦700 billion when we assumed office, we are currently running a ₦4.2 trillion budget dedicated entirely to shared prosperity, strategic empowerment and aggressively reducing unemployment through enablers like the LSETF.” The governor described the $1 trillion GDP target as ambitious but achievable, saying the state had commenced the foundational work required to attain the milestone. “As the second-largest economy in Africa, Lagos is charting an ambitious yet achievable course towards a $1 trillion GDP by 2052. Achieving this milestone will position Lagos among the leading economic sub-nationals globally, and the foundational work required to reach that destination has already begun,” he said. Sanwo-Olu also highlighted the importance of institutional continuity, citing the LSETF as an example of how successive administrations could strengthen existing programmes rather than abandon them. He noted that the fund, established a decade ago before his administration, had been strengthened and expanded to improve access to finance for small businesses and stimulate employment. According to him, the intervention has recorded a loan repayment rate of 95 per cent, disbursed funds to more than 20,000 small businesses and created over 320,000 jobs, while safeguarding another 173,000 jobs. The Commissioner for Wealth Creation and Employment, Akinyemi Ajigbotafe, said the state had impacted more than 6,500 graduates and generated over 200,000 jobs through strategic wealth creation and employment initiatives since 2023. He said the Sanwo-Olu administration remained committed to making employment opportunities accessible, sustainable and inclusive, particularly through programmes designed to equip young people with practical workplace experience. Ajigbotafe identified the Graduate Internship Placement Programme (GIPP) as one of the flagship interventions aimed at bridging the gap between academic qualifications and labour market requirements. He also described the Lagos State Job Fair as a major employment facilitation platform, noting that the 2025 and subsequent editions brought together more than 300 organisations and thousands of job seekers. The post Lagos targets $1tr GDP by 2052, Sanwo-Olu declares appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Équipe d’Algérie : la FAF va trancher sur l’avenir de Brahim Hemdani
items.description: Beaucoup d’interrogations entourent l’avenir de Brahim Hemdani et de son staff à la tête de l'équipe d'Algérie de football depuis la défaite essuyée mardi 17 novembre face au Togo (3-0) . En conférence de presse, le sélectionneur n’a rien laissé filtrer quant à ses intentions. Son avenir est en suspens. Malgré les critiques qui ciblent le staff technique, la Fédération algérienne de football (FAF) ne souhaite pas trancher dans la précipitation. Elle prendra le temps qu'il faut avant de décider, apprend-on d’une source proche de l’instance fédérale. Brahim Hemdani a été chargé de diriger la barre technique de l'équipe nationale début septembre dernier, en remplacement de Vladimir Petković, parti à l'issue du mondial 2026. La FAF a également nommé dans le staff Antar Yahia comme adjoint de l’entraîneur en chef et Moussa Saïb comme manager général de l’équipe. Bilan mitigé et interrogations sur l’avenir du staff technique de l’Algérie Le bilan du staff à la tête des Verts est mitigé, avec trois victoires, un nul et une défaite, sans avoir rencontré de grosse cylindrée. À domicile, l’équipe d’Algérie a battu sans convaincre la Zambie (3-1) et le Togo (1-0) en éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, et le Niger (2-1) en amical. À l'extérieur, les Verts ont fait match nul (2-2) au Burundi et ont perdu au Togo (3-0), dans les qualifications pour la CAN 2027. Dans cette compétition, les verts sont toujours leaders de leur groupe avec 7 points, mais avec seulement une unité d'avance sur le Togo et deux sur la Zambie. Le staff technique a à sa décharge les nombreuses blessures qui ont décimé l'effectif, mais les résultats obtenus jusque-là et les prestations de l'équipe inquiètent. D’où les interrogations sur l’avenir du staff et les rumeurs qui ont couru sur son départ après le match du Togo. Brahim Hemdani présentera son rapport dans une semaine et « des décisions seront prises » Néanmoins, la FAF ne se précipite pas. « C’est une défaite, elle ne sera pas gérée dans la précipitation », déclare à TSA une source sûre. La même source ajoute que le sélectionneur va rentrer chez lui et va présenter son rapport dans une semaine. Brahim Hemdani aura une discussion avec le président Walid Sadi et c'est à partir de là que « des décisions seront prises », indique notre source. Celle-ci rappelle que, du reste, Hemdani est « chargé de mission » à la tête de la barre technique et « s’il doit continuer, il continuera, sinon il retournera à la DTN ». Un limogeage du successeur de Petković n’est pas à écarter. Avant d'être nommé à la tête des Verts, Brahim Hemdani dirigeait la sélection U21 qu'il a menée à la victoire finale aux Jeux méditerranéens en août dernier. L’article Équipe d’Algérie : la FAF va trancher sur l’avenir de Brahim Hemdani est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Zenith Law Faculty strengthens practical training with visits to Parliament, Supreme Court
items.description: The Law Faculty of Zenith University College is expanding its practical approach to legal education through a series of institutional visits designed to expose students to the workings of key legal and governance institutions in Ghana. The programme includes educational visits to the Ghana Copyright Office, the Ghana Music Rights Organisation (GHAMRO), Parliament and the Supreme Court, providing students with opportunities to connect classroom learning with the practical application of the law. The latest initiative will see Level 300 law students visit the Ghana Copyright Office and GHAMRO on November 20, 2026, to deepen their understanding of intellectual property law and its application in professional practice. The visit, to be led by Private Legal Practitioner and Intellectual Property Law Lecturer, Mr David Olaga, is expected to expose students to the institutional processes involved in copyright administration, the protection of creative works and the management of intellectual property rights in Ghana. At the Ghana Copyright Office, students are expected to receive briefings on the institution’s mandate, the importance of intellectual property to national development and the distinction between Industrial Property and Copyright and Related Rights. The engagement will also cover the office’s responsibilities in public education, anti-counterfeiting operations, dispute resolution, advisory services and collective management. Emerging challenges in copyright enforcement, particularly digital piracy, are also expected to feature in discussions, alongside developments in digital copyright registration and international initiatives to tackle online piracy. At GHAMRO, students will be introduced to collective management systems, licensing arrangements, royalty distribution and compliance procedures. The engagement will also provide an opportunity to understand the evolution of collective rights management in Ghana, from the COSGA era to the establishment of specialised organisations such as GHAMRO, ARSOG and CopyGhana. Law students to visit Parliament and Supreme Court The intellectual property excursion forms part of a wider programme of practical learning activities being pursued by the faculty under Mr Olaga’s leadership. In a separate initiative, approximately 130 Level 200 law students are expected to visit Parliament as part of their Constitutional Law course. A letter dated November 10, 2026, addressed to the Clerk to Parliament, indicates that the proposed visit is intended to give students practical exposure to the operations of Parliament as one of the principal organs of government under the 1992 Constitution. The engagement is expected to help students appreciate the practical application of constitutional principles relating to the Legislature, separation of powers, parliamentary procedures, the legislative process and parliamentary oversight. Students are also expected to gain first-hand insight into the work of Members of Parliament, the processes involved in enacting legislation and Parliament’s role in promoting democratic governance, accountability and the rule of law. The faculty has also secured approval from the Office of the Judicial Secretary for an educational visit to the Supreme Court involving 40 Pre-Bar students and their course lecturer. According to an approval letter dated October 29, 2026, the visit is scheduled for Tuesday, November 24, at 9:30 a.m. The excursion forms part of the Skills for the Legal Profession in Ghana course and is intended to equip students with the professional knowledge, ethical values and practical understanding required for their future responsibilities as legal practitioners. The approval directs the delegation to report to the Supreme Court forecourt, where an official will receive them. Students are also required to observe the court’s security and dress protocols. Zenith places fifth in national moot court competition The faculty’s practical legal training initiatives are complemented by its performance in national legal competitions. At the Supreme Court @150 National Constitutional Moot Court Competition held on July 20 and 21, 2026, Zenith University College placed fifth overall among 11 participating law faculties, recording a score of 71.11. The performance also made the institution the second-best private law faculty in the competition. Team Zenith further won the Best Plaintiff Memorial award with a score of 82.50, presented by Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie. The university also recorded strong individual performances in the oral advocacy category, with Joseph Kobina Koomson placing fifth with 81.67 points and Nana Serwah Agyemang finishing seventh with 78.00 points. Both students secured positions among the competition’s top 10 oralists. Other members of the team included Grace Okaniokor Agordzo, Frederick Bawa, Divine Agyei and Asemfoforoba Boateng Nketiah. The achievement placed Zenith among the top-performing law faculties in the national competition and demonstrated its students’ capacity to engage in legal research, written advocacy and oral argument. Faculty builds on established legal education record Zenith University College’s Law Faculty has a history of legal education, having operated the University of London LL.B programme from 2005 to 2019, producing more than 2,000 graduates. The faculty introduced its Ghana-related LL.B programme in 2018. In the 2025 Ghana School of Law entrance examinations, the faculty recorded 41 passes out of 73 candidates, placing it among private law faculties with notable performances. The series of planned and approved institutional visits, together with the faculty’s participation in national moot court competitions, reflects an approach to legal education that extends beyond classroom lectures. By exposing students to Parliament, the Supreme Court and institutions responsible for intellectual property administration, the faculty seeks to strengthen their understanding of how legal principles operate in practice and prepare them for the professional demands of the legal sector. The November 20 intellectual property excursion is expected to provide another opportunity for students to connect academic knowledge with the work of institutions shaping Ghana’s legal and creative industries.

items.title: KNUST launches AI winter school to advance responsible healthcare innovation in Africa
items.description: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has launched a winter school focused on developing responsible, African-led artificial intelligence solutions for healthcare, with researchers already testing AI tools to support stroke diagnosis using brain scans from Ghanaian patients. The RAIL-DATAIA Winter School, organised by the university’s Responsible Artificial Intelligence Lab (RAIL), brings together researchers, students, health professionals and international partners from Ghana and France to explore practical applications of AI in healthcare. The programme forms part of the Africa Forward AI Clusters initiative, a collaboration between African universities and French institutions aimed at strengthening AI research, training and entrepreneurship across the continent. Speaking at the launch, RAIL Scientific Director, Professor Jerry John Kponyo, said AI could help extend the reach of health professionals, particularly in rural and underserved communities where access to specialists and healthcare facilities remains limited. He stressed that the technology should support rather than replace doctors and nurses, enabling health workers to serve more patients, work efficiently and make better-informed clinical decisions. Professor Kponyo cited Ghana’s doctor-to-patient ratio as one reason for exploring technological solutions to the pressure on the health system. “The doctor-to-patient ratio in our health system is about one to ten thousand, and so there is the need for us to get some technologies to assist with reference to the number of people that we are taking care of, and that is where AI finds expression also,” he said. He said AI could support triage, early disease detection, remote consultations and clinical decision-making, especially for patients who have to travel long distances to access specialist care. KNUST researchers test AI for stroke diagnosis Professor Kponyo disclosed that KNUST researchers were testing AI applications on brain scans from Ghanaian patients to support the diagnosis of stroke in hospitals with limited access to radiologists. He said the ability of AI systems to analyse large volumes of medical information could help health workers identify diseases earlier, improve diagnosis and support timely treatment. He also pointed to opportunities for applying AI in the discovery and treatment of diseases, although he cautioned that healthcare applications must be developed with appropriate safeguards. “A health AI trained on data that does not reflect our people will fail our people. For that matter, health technologies must keep clinicians and patients at the centre of decision-making and be accessible to communities beyond major teaching hospitals,” he said. He called for fairness, transparency and accountability in the development of health technologies, alongside strong protections for patients’ privacy and dignity. KNUST pushes for African-led AI development Professor Kponyo said the Africa Forward AI Clusters initiative was intended to strengthen the continent’s capacity to develop its own AI systems and translate research into commercial applications. “The purpose of the clusters is to develop sovereign AI designed and trained in Africa and to bridge the gap between African scientific talent and commercial success,” he said. The initiative involves six countries: Kenya, Benin, Ghana, Morocco, Egypt and South Africa. It supports talent development, academic exchanges, research commercialisation and joint innovation challenges. Speaking on behalf of the Vice-Chancellor and the university community, Acting Pro Vice-Chancellor Professor Kwabena Biritwum Nyarko said the Winter School demonstrated the value of international research partnerships in addressing local and global challenges. He said KNUST, through RAIL, had contributed to the development of Ghana’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy. Professor Nyarko urged African countries to move beyond adopting technologies developed elsewhere and build the expertise needed to develop and govern solutions that respond to their own priorities. “AI sovereignty does not mean technological isolation. It means building the capacity to develop our own solutions, protect our interests, and engage the global AI ecosystem from a position of knowledge and strength,” he said. He encouraged researchers to consider affordability, accessibility, the availability of local data and the capacity to scale up AI applications when developing healthcare solutions. Ghana-France partnership emphasises balanced collaboration Representing the French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space, Nathalie Nilsson-Thiello called for partnerships that reflect the priorities and interests of all participating institutions. “Our partnerships must be balanced and close-knit. They must address both our own priorities and those of our partners,” she said. She advocated joint research programmes, reciprocal academic mobility and stronger links between education, research and innovation. Ms Nilsson-Thiello also highlighted the importance of involving young people and participants from the public and private sectors to sustain the collaboration. The Winter School programme covers AI applications in rare disease diagnosis, therapeutic HPV vaccine discovery, climate-resilient public health and the detection of ischaemic stroke.

items.title: Actes antichrétiens : la France confirme sa place de championne d’Europe
items.description: Dans son dernier rapport annuel, « Intolerance et discrimination envers les chretiens en Europe 2026 », paru ce 16 novembre, l'Observatoire de l'intolerance et des discriminations envers les chretiens en Europe (OIDAC) a recense 2 465 « crimes et incidents de haine antichretiens » en 2025 en Europe, contre 2 211 en 2024. Les pays ou ces actes ont ete les plus eleves sont la France, avec 843 actes antichretiens recenses en 2025 par le ministere francais de l'Interieur, suivi de l'Angleterre et le Pays de Galles, avec 624 actes antichretiens, puis loin derriere l'Allemagne avec 337 actes, ferme ce podium. Toutefois, concernant l'Allemagne – et entendant mettre « en lumiere d'importantes lacunes dans l'enregistrement et le signalement » des actes antichretiens –, l'OIDAC a souligne que les autorites allemandes les mettaient dans le meme sac que « les crimes a motivation politique ». « Depuis quinze ans que l'on fait cette etude, la France est toujours en tete, et reste a un niveau eleve », a commente Anja Tang, directrice de cette ONG basee a Vienne, citee par Le Figaro . « Mais ce qui est frappant cette annee, c'est le nombre d'atteintes aux personnes, qui y augmente encore plus qu'en Europe ! Nous sommes inquiets pour la securite des fideles et des membres du clerge en France ». Les agressions physiques en hausse de 44 % sur un an Des agressions sur lesquelles s'attarde le rapport de l'OIDAC. Si la plupart des incidents recenses « continuent de viser des eglises et autres lieux de culte chretiens, notamment des incendies criminels, des actes de vandalisme et des profanations », est-il souligne, les agressions recensees contre des personnes « ont augmente de 44 % par rapport a 2024 », avec 395 agressions contre des personnes en 2025 contre 274 agressions l'annee precedente. Un phenomene qui, la encore, concerne particulierement la France ou « les infractions contre les personnes ont augmente de 70 %, les violences physiques visant les membres de la communaute chretienne ont double et les agressions physiques contre le clerge et les autres responsables religieux ont quadruple », peut-on lire. Parmi ces violences, l'OIDAC met en avant l'assassinat en septembre 2025 a Lyon, d'Ashur Sarnaya, un chretien assyrien qui avait fui les persecutions islamistes en Irak. Handicape de naissance, il avait ete poignarde a mort dans son fauteuil roulant par un ressortissant algerien en lien avec Daesh alors qu'il diffusait en direct des messages chretiens. Le Parquet national antiterroriste francais avait mis un mois a se saisir du dossier.

items.title: NRSA boss announces tougher enforcement as Upper West records alarming road deaths
items.description: The Director-General of the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA), Abraham Amaliba, has warned that he is prepared to lose his job to enforce a directive barring political parties from placing campaign posters on road signs. He issued the warning during a regional engagement in Wa, where he announced a series of measures to address road safety concerns, including the removal of traders from road pavements, the introduction of technology-driven traffic enforcement and mandatory towing of broken-down vehicles. Mr Amaliba said following engagements with ministers, local government authorities had been given a one-month ultimatum to clear traders and commercial activities from road spaces and pavements. He also announced plans to issue directives requiring political parties to stop placing campaign posters on road signs, warning that the practice obstructs visibility and poses a danger to road users. Emphasising his determination to enforce the directive, he said he was willing to lose his job rather than allow the practice to continue. The NRSA Director-General outlined the authority’s road safety framework, which is built around the “Four E’s” of Education, Enforcement, Engineering and Emergency Response. He also urged motorists to observe the COAT principle – Concentration, Observation, Attention and Tolerance – while driving. Mr Amaliba said that although the NRSA would intensify public education and sensitisation, effective enforcement required close collaboration with the police, stressing that education alone would not guarantee compliance without appropriate sanctions. Police target private vehicles amid rising road fatalities The urgency of the interventions was highlighted during a briefing at the Upper West Regional Police Headquarters by the Regional Police Commander, DCOP Francis Yiribaare. He disclosed that the police were shifting their enforcement strategies to pay greater attention to private vehicles, which he said were increasingly becoming a road safety concern despite their relatively low passenger capacity. DCOP Yiribaare reported that recent fatal crashes in the region had claimed the lives of 22 males and 11 females. He identified over-speeding as the leading cause of road fatalities, particularly along the Wa-Tumu stretch. Among the incidents he recounted were a fatal tyre burst that claimed the lives of a mother and her children, as well as a crash that killed the senior auditor of Tumu Training College. The Regional Commander also highlighted efforts by the police to address interference from influential individuals in the enforcement of road traffic regulations. He said officers had intensified public education, including engagements with congregants at local mosques, to sensitise chiefs and community leaders on road safety and encourage them to support law enforcement. According to him, the approach has helped reduce interference in police operations, with community leaders increasingly allowing officers to carry out their duties when offenders are arrested. DCOP Yiribaare said his officers enforced the law “without favouritism or fear”, adding that even his own colleagues had never requested special treatment for relatives who committed traffic offences. NRSA introduces technology-driven enforcement, mandatory towing Addressing the concerns raised by the police, Mr Amaliba called for a modernised approach to traffic enforcement and announced the introduction of a system known as Trafitech. The system uses cameras to automate traffic monitoring and enforcement, reducing direct human involvement in identifying and apprehending traffic offenders. He said the initiative was being rolled out in Accra and Kumasi, with plans to extend it to other parts of the country to improve compliance and discourage reckless driving. Mr Amaliba also announced that from next year, the towing of broken-down vehicles from roads would become mandatory to prevent crashes involving stationary vehicles. He said the measure would particularly target heavy-duty vehicles operating in the northern parts of the country, including Sahelian transport trucks, which frequently break down and remain abandoned on highways for extended periods. Ghana records at least eight road deaths daily – NRSA The scale of Ghana’s road safety challenge was further highlighted by the NRSA’s Deputy Director for Planning and Programming, Dennis Yeribu, during a stakeholder engagement. Mr Yeribu disclosed that Ghana records at least 38 road crashes, eight deaths and 45 permanent injuries every day. He said men account for 80 per cent of road crash fatalities, while nearly 90 per cent of those killed are adults aged 18 and above. According to him, the period between 2:00 pm and 8:00 pm is particularly dangerous for road users, with 3,644 fatalities recorded within the six-hour window between 2015 and 2024. He further indicated that the Upper West Region records crash severity rates above the national average, with motorcycle-related fatalities contributing significantly to the country’s road safety challenges. Mr Yeribu also cited a 26 per cent national increase in motorcycle fatalities, underscoring the need for stronger enforcement and targeted road safety interventions. The engagements form part of efforts by the NRSA and its partners to strengthen road safety enforcement, improve public awareness and reduce preventable deaths and injuries on Ghana’s roads.

items.title: KP governor forms 8-member commission to probe illegal placer gold mining
items.description: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Wednesday constituted an eight-member inquiry commission to probe illegal placer gold mining in the province. The commission, according to a notification issued by the provincial home and tribal affairs department, will be headed by retired Justice Asadullah Khan Chamkani. It will also include as members Barrister Mohammad Yaseen Raza, legal adviser/member Sher Akbar Khan, Deputy Inspector General of Police Wasif Rahman, Health Department Additional Secretary Engineer Ziarat Khan, and representatives of intelligence agencies. According to the notification, the commission will inquire into the extent, history and nature of illegal placer gold mining in KP, particularly in Kohat, Nowshera, Karak and other affected districts. The inquiry includes the scale, duration and locations of illegal operations. In addition to this, the commission will identify persons, groups and networks involved in illegal mining, including beneficiaries, and determine their “respective roles, financial gains and individual or institutional responsibility for facilitation, corruption, negligence, abuse of authority or failure to discharge legal duties”. Similarly, it will also inquire into “allegations of patronage, facilitation and connivance by political figures, public representatives, government functionaries, law enforcement personnel or any other persons or institutions, including corruption, abuse of authority, deliberate inaction or protection provided to illegal mining operations”, the notification said. The commission will also examine the financial dimensions of illegal mining, including the estimated quantity and value of gold illegally extracted, losses caused to the public exchequer, movement of proceeds, money laundering, smuggling and possible links with organised crime, terrorist groups or terrorist financing. It will additionally examine the role and performance of concerned government departments, district administrations and the police in “preventing illegal mining, monitoring lease conditions, taking enforcement action, registering and investigating cases, prosecuting offenders and dealing with seized machinery, gold and other property”. The commission has also been tasked to determine the reasons for the continuation or recurrence of illegal mining in spite of repeated complaints, government directions, enforcement operations and criminal proceedings, including negligence, deliberate failure to enforce the law, interference or facilitation by those responsible for enforcement. In addition to this, it will also inquire into the circumstances surrounding the Kohat incident of Nov 11 , including any links between illegal mining networks and the attack on police personnel, possible planning, financing, facilitation or support, and any relevant operational or security lapses, without prejudice to ongoing criminal investigations, the notification said. Eighteen terrorists were killed while 10 cops were martyred on Nov 11 when a police team came under attack on its way back after completing an operation against elements involved in illegal gold mining. The committee will also examine previous inquiries, reports, complaints and decisions, including those of the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), Provincial Cabinet Inquiry Committee (PCIC) and other competent authorities, assess the implementation of their findings and recommendations, and examine any fresh material or evidence warranting further inquiry. The commission will assess the financial and environmental damage caused by illegal mining, including loss of government revenue and damage to riverbeds and adjoining areas, while identifying persons or entities against whom recovery, compensation or other legal action may be warranted. It will also recommend specific action against those found responsible, including criminal investigation or prosecution, departmental proceedings, recovery of unlawful gains or public losses, and any other action warranted under the applicable laws. It will also recommend immediate measures, wherever necessary, for preservation of evidence, protection of witnesses and records, securing public assets and preventing interference with the inquiry. The commission will submit a comprehensive report containing its findings, supporting evidence and the responsibility of persons or institutions concerned, as well as specific recommendations for further action by the competent authorities. “The commission may examine any person, record, transaction, lease, operation or incident relevant to its mandate, irrespective of the period involved or the position or status of the persons concerned,” the notification added. It added that the inquiry would not be confined to any particular government, department, institution or category of persons. According to the notification, the commission will be given access to all relevant material, including a confidential report received from the Prime Minister’s Office vide a letter dated Aug 25, the chief secretary’s directions of Sept 8, NAB and PCIC reports, relevant cabinet decisions, departmental files, lease and auction records, complaints, first information reports, investigation and prosecution records, machinery seizure and release records, and any other material relevant to the inquiry. “The commission shall exercise the powers available under the West Pakistan Tribunals of Inquiry Ordinance, 1969, including summoning and examining witnesses on oath, requiring the production of records and documents, receiving evidence, calling for information from any person or authority, requisitioning public records and conducting proceedings in accordance with law,” the notification read. According to the notification, the KP Mines and Minerals Development Department will provide secretarial, administrative and logistical support to the commission. The commission will submit its report to the KP governor within 45 days of its notification. The probe has been set up in the aftermath of an attack that led to the martyrdom of 10 police personnel in the Gumbat area of Kohat district on Nov 11 while they were returning from an operation against illegal placer gold mining along the Indus River. The incident came a day after the Kohat deputy commissioner imposed a 60-day ban on parking excavators within blocks C and D of placer gold mining areas and adjoining locations. According to the order, these could easily be used for unauthorised gold extraction. Condemning the attack, Kundi on Saturday announced a ban on gold mining across the province and the revocation of all mining leases as part of measures to curb illegal mining.

items.title: Météo-Tunisie | Ciel voilé et vents forts près des côtes cette nuit
items.description: Selon les prévisions de l'Institut national de la météorologie (INM), un temps sera voilé sur l'ensemble du territoire cette nuit, accompagné de rafales soutenues par endroits. L'INM précise que les vents souffleront fort près des côtes nord, tandis qu'ils demeureront faibles à modérés dans les autres zones avec une mer très agitée au nord et peu agitée à agitée sur le reste du littoral tunisien. Quant aux températures, la même source annonce des nocturnes en légère baisse, variant entre 14 et 19 °C Y. N. items.title: Burkina Faso : L’ADCT finance à hauteur de près de 49 millions F CFA la construction d’un 2e centre d’éveil préscolaire à Sindou
items.description: La commune de Sindou dispose désormais d’un deuxième centre d’éveil et d’éducation préscolaire (CEEP), doté d’infrastructures adaptées à l’accueil des tout-petits. Réalisé grâce à un financement de près de 49 millions de F CFA de l’Agence nationale d’appui au développement des collectivités territoriales (ADCT), le centre a été officiellement inauguré ce 18 novembre 2026, en présence des journalistes participant à la caravane de presse organisée par l’ADCT. Cette inauguration marque l’aboutissement d’une attente des acteurs de l’éducation préscolaire et des populations de Sindou. Selon Yadia Issiaka, président de la délégation spéciale de la commune, le centre fonctionnait auparavant dans un local d’emprunt qui ne répondait pas aux conditions d’accueil des enfants. « Aujourd’hui, le centre dispose d’un cadre sain, sécurisé et propice à l’épanouissement des tout-petits avant leur entrée au primaire » , a-t-il déclaré. Il a également souligné que cette nouvelle infrastructure permet d’accroître la capacité d’accueil du préscolaire dans la commune et d’offrir aux parents un cadre adapté pour la scolarisation de leurs enfants. Un investissement de près de 49 millions de FCFA-©Faso7 D’un coût total de 48 975 913 F CFA, le projet a été entièrement financé par l’ADCT. Il porte sur la construction d’un bloc de trois salles de classe équipées, d’un bureau, d’un magasin, d’une clôture et d’une latrine à trois postes. La maîtrise d’ouvrage a été assurée par la commune de Sindou. Pour la Directrice générale de l’ADCT, Donbeyitwor Jeanne-Marie Raïssa Yaméogo/Dabiré, cet investissement répond à un besoin exprimé par les populations et traduit la volonté de renforcer l’offre éducative dans la commune. Elle a rappelé que la petite enfance constitue une période déterminante dans l’acquisition des premières aptitudes intellectuelles, sociales et comportementales. « Investir dans la petite enfance, c’est bâtir les hommes de demain » , a-t-elle affirmé lors de son entretien avec la presse. Elle a exprimé sa satisfaction de voir l’infrastructure achevée, estimant que l’accompagnement technique et financier de l’ADCT a permis à la collectivité de répondre à une forte demande en matière d’éducation préscolaire. Le chef de la circonscription d’éducation de base (CCEB) de Sindou, Emmanuel Sourabié, a également salué la réalisation de ce centre, qu’il considère comme un acquis pour les enfants et les acteurs de l’éducation. Il a insisté sur l’importance du préscolaire dans la préparation des enfants à leur entrée au cours préparatoire première année (CP1). « La plus belle richesse, ce n’est pas de l’argent. C’est un enfant éduqué » , a-t-il déclaré, avant d’inviter les parents à inscrire leurs enfants dès l’âge de trois ou quatre ans. Selon lui, le passage par le préscolaire facilite l’apprentissage des premières notions, la maîtrise du crayon, l’écoute et la vie en communauté. Un appel à l’appropriation et à l’entretien du centre-©Faso7 Au-delà de la mise à disposition des locaux, les intervenants ont insisté sur la nécessité d’assurer leur bonne utilisation et leur pérennité. Le président de la délégation spéciale a invité les enseignants à faire bon usage de l’infrastructure et les parents à accompagner le personnel éducatif dans sa mission. La Directrice générale de l’ADCT a, pour sa part, rappelé que la réalisation d’un équipement ne suffit pas à garantir son efficacité. Sa préservation et son bon fonctionnement nécessitent l’implication des autorités communales, des éducateurs, des parents et de l’ensemble de la communauté. Dans le même sens, le secrétaire général de la province, Somé Yourviel, a appelé les populations à considérer le centre comme un bien commun. Il a exhorté les différents acteurs à protéger les équipements, à entretenir régulièrement les locaux et à encourager les inscriptions. La construction du CEEP de Niofila bientôt achevée-©Faso7 Avec ce deuxième CEEP, la commune de Sindou renforce son dispositif d’accueil préscolaire. Le défi reste désormais de faire vivre cette infrastructure, en assurant sa fréquentation, la qualité de l’encadrement et la préservation des équipements au bénéfice des jeunes enfants. En marge de cette inauguration, la directrice générale de l’ADCT a également effectué une visite du chantier de construction du nouveau centre d’éveil et d’éducation préscolaire (CEEP) de Niofila, dans la commune de Douna. Cette infrastructure, destinée à remplacer les anciens locaux devenus vétustes et inadaptés, comprend trois salles de classe équipées, un bureau, un magasin, une clôture et une latrine à trois postes. D’un coût total de 44 368 033 FCFA, entièrement financé par l’ADCT, le projet vise à améliorer les conditions d’accueil et d’apprentissage des enfants. Les travaux étaient au stade des finitions au moment de la visite. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : L’ADCT finance à hauteur de près de 49 millions F CFA la construction d’un 2e centre d’éveil préscolaire à Sindou est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Primaire de la droite et du centre : «On doit lui mettre la pression», estime David Lisnard à l’endroit d’Édouard Philippe
items.description: « edouard Philippe, c'est indispensable ». Convie le 18 novembre sur un plateau de TF1, au lendemain d'une rencontre entre ses equipes et celles de Gabriel Attal et Bruno Retailleau, en vue de l'organisation courant janvier d'une primaire , le candidat Nouvelle energie a la presidentielle, David Lisnard, a presente comme une « condition » la participation de cet autre ex-Premier ministre macroniste a cette primaire. Un exercice auquel le principal interesse a, jusqu'a present, refuse de participer, estimant qu'une primaire dans son camp politique tiendrait de la « confusion » et de la « division ». « C'est pour cela qu'on doit lui mettre la pression », a ajoute le maire de Cannes, « dire qu'on accepterait de faire la competition sans lui, c'est lui permettre de rester tranquille sur son Aventin ». « Est-ce qu'on s'affronte avant pour avoir une chance d'etre au deuxieme tour, ou est-ce qu'on s'affronte au premier tour », a developpe celui qui monte dans les intentions de vote. David Lisnard, comme tous ses concurrents dans l'espace politique allant de Marine Le Pen a Jean-Luc Melenchon, sont aujourd'hui donnes par les sondages comme etant elimines des le premier tour de la presidentielle qui doit se tenir le 18 avril 2027. Dans son discours, David Lisnard presente la primaire comme un exercice visant a faire trancher les electeurs et ainsi eviter des « compromissions » sur les programmes de chacun dans le cadre d'une alliance negociee. Du cote d'edouard Philippe, encore credite d'une legere avance sur ses concurrents – et dorenavant talonne par David Lisnard – on joue cette courte tete afin d'appeler les autres candidats a se rallier sous la banniere Horizons. En perte de vitesse, edouard Philippe a presente ce 18 novembre son programme « massif » pour la France. Dans celui-ci, on retrouve une fibre liberale, avec notamment la suppression des 35 heures et des mesures visant la fonction publique, ou encore des retraites qui reposeraient en partie sur une capitalisation, ainsi qu'une fibre intrinsequement pro-Bruxelles et pro-Kiev . Un aspect, qu'aux dernieres nouvelles, ne partagent pas forcement – ou du moins a ce niveau – Bruno Retailleau ou David Lisnard.

items.title: Festival de Marrakech : Une société algérienne impose le retrait d’un film malgré l’opposition du réalisateur
items.description: À deux jours de l’ouverture de sa 23ᵉ édition, le Festival international du film de Marrakech est confronté au retrait d’un film de sa compétition officielle. La société de production algérienne « Isaad Film Productions », détentrice des droits de « Chroniques d’un temps de siège », du réalisateur palestino-syrien Abdallah Al-Khatib, a décidé de retirer l’œuvre de la sélection, malgré l’opposition affichée du cinéaste. Dans un communiqué, le festival indique avoir été informé de cette décision, alors que la participation du long-métrage avait été confirmée dès le 1ᵉʳ juin dernier, date à laquelle les producteurs avaient donné leur accord pour sa sélection. Le réalisateur a, de son côté, exprimé son « opposition totale » à ce retrait, tant auprès des producteurs que de la direction du festival. Il a également fait part de son souhait de maintenir la projection de son film à Marrakech. Cette décision concerne une œuvre qui avait pourtant bénéficié de l’accompagnement du festival. En 2024, « Chroniques d’un temps de siège » avait été soutenu par les Ateliers de l’Atlas, le programme de développement des talents du Festival international du film de Marrakech destiné aux réalisateurs et producteurs du Maroc, du monde arabe et d’Afrique. Le film y avait obtenu le Prix de l’Atlas dans la catégorie postproduction. En février dernier, il avait également été sélectionné au Festival international du film de Berlin, où il avait remporté le prix du meilleur premier long-métrage de fiction. Malgré les démarches du réalisateur pour maintenir la projection, le festival affirme être tenu de respecter la décision de la société détentrice des droits de l’œuvre. Il indique, en conséquence, ne pas être en mesure de conserver le film dans sa programmation. La 23ᵉ édition du Festival international du film de Marrakech se tiendra du 20 au 28 novembre 2026. Au total, 76 films issus de 39 pays seront présentés dans les différentes sections de la manifestation : la compétition officielle, les séances de gala, les horizons, le 11ᵉ continent, le panorama du cinéma marocain, les projections destinées au jeune public et aux familles, ainsi que les films inscrits dans le cadre des hommages de cette édition. Dix de ces œuvres seront présentées en première mondiale. Douze films de la sélection ont, par ailleurs, bénéficié du soutien des Ateliers de l’Atlas, le programme du festival dédié à l’industrie cinématographique et au développement des talents.
