items.title: Gaming phenomenon 'Grand Theft Auto' goes live after 13-year wait
items.description: After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing on Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed. “GTA VI” becomes available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight on Thursday in each region where it will be available. That meant it launched first in New Zealand (at 1100 GMT or 4pm PKT on Wednesday), with many players around the world changing their console location settings to the far-eastern country to be among the first to enter the new Vice City. “I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time that the anticipation for this is crazy,” Australian student Riley Fennel told AFP ahead of the launch. Although Rockstar Games, the studio behind GTA, has not yet released advance unit sales figures, specialist firm Sensor Tower estimates they have already surpassed 15 million. That would be more than $1.5bn in revenue before the game even came out, for a budget estimated at $1bn to $1.5bn, which would be unprecedented. According to the British analytics firm Omdia, sales of “GTA VI” could reach $3.2bn by the end of the year. ‘Taylor Swift of games’ “No other concert or box office release has ever generated that much capital. And so that makes it one of the outliers in entertainment,” said Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” the industry specialist said. Rockstar’s parent company, US publisher Take-Two Interactive, has rolled out a massive marketing campaign to establish the title as a mass cultural product that transcends the boundaries of video games. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said James McWhirter at Omdia. “I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning this first game session “for a very long time”. Like him, many fans have already booked time off to immerse themselves in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida. The human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 per cent increase in leave requests around the world for Nov 19. Touted as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows the adventures of a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in the Miami-inspired, crime-ravaged Vice City. Since its beginnings, the series has won players over with its increasingly realistic reconstructions of fictionalised cities and the great freedom of action offered in a highly detailed open world. Gamers entering GTA’s worlds can drive cars, fly planes or go skydiving. “GTA VI” promises to push its realism even further, with characters looking different depending on what they eat and players having to work at cultivating the relationship between the protagonists. Ahead of its release, the game picked up eight nominations on Tuesday at the Game Awards, the American ceremony that will honour the best video games of the year on Dec 10. Subversion and controversy Rockstar, which by 2026 will have a dozen studios around the world and more than 4,700 employees, devoted more than eight years to building the latest GTA instalment. Active production only began after the release of Rockstar’s previous game, “Red Dead Redemption II”, in 2018. It was a rocky ride to release. Shaken by a series of leaks in 2022 and the online release of stolen gameplay videos, the studio postponed the launch twice, then suffered a new round of leaks last summer. The games have also regularly been accused of glorifying violence and illegal behaviour as GTA has carved out a place in pop culture as a symbol of subversion, unafraid to mock the flaws of American society. Players can run over pedestrians, sell drugs and shoot at the police. “It’s a series that is famous for being always over the top in terms of its representation of violence and different forms of abuse or harassment, for its representations of gender”, said Paolo Ruffino, a lecturer in digital cultures at King’s College London. “I don’t expect to see necessarily major controversies unless there is something completely new,” he added. But as a consequence of its scandalous legacy, several countries have banned the saga. No official release is currently planned in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

items.title: Ukraine: From reactive response to a culture of care [EN/UK]
items.description: Country: Ukraine Source: Prosper Global Please refer to the attached files. Institutionalizing Duty of Care for local partners in Ukraine Local organizations deliver a large share of the humanitarian response in Ukraine, often closest to the front line and with the fewest protections. This report documents how Prosper Global (formerly Mercy Corps) in Ukraine moved from ad hoc, reactive support to an institutionalized Duty of Care Minimum Package for its local partners between 2022 and 2025. It sets out the nine options available to partners, how the package was embedded into partnership systems, what partners prioritized and which gaps remain. Key takeaway is that Duty of Care for partners works best when it is non-negotiable as a standard, yet flexible, risk-based and partner-led in its application. Why Duty of Care matters Humanitarian work in Ukraine is carried out under persistent threat. Aid workers and volunteers operate within range of artillery, missiles and drones. Offices and homes are damaged in attacks on cities far from the front line, and repeated strikes on energy infrastructure leave teams without power, heating and connectivity for hours or days. Constant air-raid alerts add a layer of cumulative stress that rarely disappears. Local civil society organizations carry a disproportionate share of this risk. They are often the first to reach affected communities and the last to leave, yet they typically work with small teams, mixed employment arrangements and limited access to insurance, security expertise or psychosocial support. Shifting leadership to local actors without ensuring their protection transfers risk rather than power. Prosper Global works in Ukraine primarily through partnerships, collaborating with around 35 local partners across humanitarian response, economic recovery, agriculture and energy resilience. A partner organization is not an aid-delivery channel but a community of professionals whose safety and well-being are integral to the success of the humanitarian mission.

items.title: South Sudan - Concept of Operations, November 2026
items.description: Country: South Sudan Sources: Logistics Cluster, World Food Programme Please refer to the attached file. Summary Humanitarian logistics operations in South Sudan continue to face significant access constraints driven by inadequate road infrastructure, seasonal flooding, insecurity and deterioration of key supply routes. Renewed conflict and localized insecurity further disrupt humanitarian supply chains, while much of the road network remains unpaved and highly vulnerable to seasonal deterioration. During the rainy season, critical routes frequently become impassable, resulting in delivery delays, higher transport costs and increased reliance on costlier alternative transport modalities. These constraints are particularly acute in Jonglei, Unity and Upper Nile, where poor road conditions, flooding and insecurity continue to restrict last-mile delivery to vulnerable and hard-to-reach communities. Despite ongoing improvements by humanitarian, government and private-sector actors, significant access gaps persist, underscoring the need for sustained donor investment in early prepositioning, coordinated access planning, critical route rehabilitation and maintenance, and common logistics services to improve cost-efficiency, reduce supply disruptions and ensure timely delivery of life-saving assistance.

items.title: Comment rendre disponibles les engrais sur le continent africain?
items.description: Dans un contexte international perturbé par les guerres au Moyen-Orient et en Ukraine, la fondation FARM (Fondation pour l'agriculture et la ruralité dans le monde) vient de publier une étude inédite : un baromètre des engrais sur le continent africain. Parmi les chiffres clés : 65% des terres arables africaines sont dégradées, et 24 pays appliquent moins de 10 kilos d'engrais par hectare, quand les agriculteurs en utilisent en moyenne 135 kilos dans le monde. Dans le même temps, l'Afrique exporte plus de 80% des engrais qu'elle produit sur son sol.
